00dfb034-7745-571e-9003-aff48bf346d0.name: Talismanic necklace
00dfb034-7745-571e-9003-aff48bf346d0.type: Amulet; cultic object; talismanic object; jewellery
00dfb034-7745-571e-9003-aff48bf346d0.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
00dfb034-7745-571e-9003-aff48bf346d0.author: Huda Kilani
00dfb034-7745-571e-9003-aff48bf346d0.keywords: Talisman; triangular; silver; pendant; Ottoman coins; heal of Gazalle; coin; coinage; currency; numismatics
00dfb034-7745-571e-9003-aff48bf346d0.description2: A triangular silver pendant decorated with small circles on the top and five blue beads with five silver Ottoman coins dangling at the end, and a silver chain known traditionally as “heal of gazelle”. Silver was the most common jewellery. The dowry of silver and gold jewellery was given by the groom to the bride, reflecting the financial status of the groom.

02c23c32-bafe-5d35-af62-5391f4a033ad.name: The Coffee Shop of Cairo
02c23c32-bafe-5d35-af62-5391f4a033ad.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
02c23c32-bafe-5d35-af62-5391f4a033ad.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
02c23c32-bafe-5d35-af62-5391f4a033ad.description2: This colourful print depicts a typical 19th century coffeeshop in Cairo. An exclusively male domain, its design was characterised by an open front and wide benches for seating, to allow for easy congregation and the gathering of friends and acquainances. Not only in Cairo, which had over a thousands coffeehouses in Roberts's time, but all over the Middle East, coffeehouses were important social hubs for the exchange of news, entertainment, smoking (customers brought their own pipes and waterpipes) and - not rarely - political dissent. Musicians and storytellers often enhanced the experience further. In this image, the proprietor or an employee of the cafe can be seen serving a beverage in the centre. Interestingly, both the ewer and the large copper cup he uses are of a type usually associated with water, not coffee. Perhaps Roberts introduced these items for artistic effect.
02c23c32-bafe-5d35-af62-5391f4a033ad.artist_birthplace: David Roberts: Edinburgh, Scotland; Louis Hague: Tournai, Belgium
02c23c32-bafe-5d35-af62-5391f4a033ad.artist_deathplace: David Roberts: London; Louis Hague: London

03fa93d0-4ba6-5345-9362-3c66f5efb5d1.name: Necklace
03fa93d0-4ba6-5345-9362-3c66f5efb5d1.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
03fa93d0-4ba6-5345-9362-3c66f5efb5d1.keywords: zebra fish; concave; Ottoman; coins; silver
03fa93d0-4ba6-5345-9362-3c66f5efb5d1.description2: A zebra fish chain with a concave silver Turkish coins and two metal circles at the end to fix the necklace on the hat and dangle down the neck. Silver was the most common jewellery. The dowry of silver and gold jewellery was given by the groom to the bride, reflecting the financial status of the groom. Jordan's economy relied on trade and crafts; new waves of people started to come to Jordan and began to settle for these purposes. This object reflects the diverse population composition of Jordan in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. It also demonstrates personal attire, fashion, local costumes and rites.

044d3688-09a9-5686-9435-b466fd271998.name: A photograph of the last Ottoman celebration of Nabi Musa feast
044d3688-09a9-5686-9435-b466fd271998.third_name: *Last Turkish Celebration of Nebi Musa feast*

04c6becd-fdd7-5c20-9596-b48f8a6ce25a.name: Traditional bridal costume and jewellery
04c6becd-fdd7-5c20-9596-b48f8a6ce25a.author: Gordanche Vidinic, ethnologist
04c6becd-fdd7-5c20-9596-b48f8a6ce25a.keywords: Costume; accessories; headdress; fez; wedding; marriage
04c6becd-fdd7-5c20-9596-b48f8a6ce25a.description2: This set of traditional clothing gives an overall picture of the universally recognized aesthetics displayed in the festive women’s outfits in Macedonia in the 19th century. Bridal costumes worn in the area of Dolni Polog were distinctive for the great number of varied garments they comprised. The costume, consisting of a *fusta*, a kind of undershirt; a *bunda*, a thicker undergarment; chemise; tunic; vest and other garments, was abundantly decorated with embroidery. It was also richly embellished with jewellery and accessorized with distinctive headdress. Even the headdress included more than one article: a fez made of red baize, a hair band called a *votus* adorned with strings of coins as well as a transparent silk scarf decorated with embroidery, fringes and sequins.

04e56c00-ff8a-5334-9dea-eb0e9fc10644.name: *Kjustek* for men's watch
04e56c00-ff8a-5334-9dea-eb0e9fc10644.author: Milena Petrovic, ethnologist
04e56c00-ff8a-5334-9dea-eb0e9fc10644.keywords: Men's jewellery; kjustek; metalwork; accessories; silver; filigree
04e56c00-ff8a-5334-9dea-eb0e9fc10644.second_name: Men's ornament worn on the chests
04e56c00-ff8a-5334-9dea-eb0e9fc10644.description2: Unlike the diversity of women’s jewellery, there was smaller number of articles of adornment used by men. Male jewellery was, however, rather massive, more precious and more costly in its production. Besides rings, especially impressive were massive silver *kjusteks* (watch chains), which were worn suspended on the chests. This *kjustek* is a nice piece of the jewellery worn by men, showing clearly some elements of Oriental influence. *Kjusteks* and other pieces of metal jewellery used to be worn by men in towns, whereas the jewellery of men in villages was mostly made of tiny beads (*monistra*).

05d7791f-fc59-5e62-bfee-252400caeca3.name: Portrait of Shaykh 'Abd al-Basit al-Fakhuri
05d7791f-fc59-5e62-bfee-252400caeca3.description: Born in Beirut in 1824, Shaykh 'Abd al-Basit al-Fakhuri studied under great masters such as Shaykh Muhammad al-Hur in the Great Umari Mosque in Beirut. He quickly gained a brilliant reputation and begun teaching before the age of 25. He remained a mufti until his death in 1905. Many of his manuscripts, and a book on *hadith* were found, unpublished, after his death.
05d7791f-fc59-5e62-bfee-252400caeca3.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Hassan El Masri, Remy Nader

077c68fe-2e6b-58e1-8e7b-c457e2fe3a33.name: Belt of *monistra* – tiny beads
077c68fe-2e6b-58e1-8e7b-c457e2fe3a33.author: Milena Petrovic, ethnologist
077c68fe-2e6b-58e1-8e7b-c457e2fe3a33.keywords: Monistra – tiny beads in different colours; costume; accessories
077c68fe-2e6b-58e1-8e7b-c457e2fe3a33.description2: Unlike the metal jewellery worn in towns, which was produced by goldsmiths, jewellery and other articles of adornment from rural areas were made by women themselves, mostly of canvas, *monistra* (tiny beads in varied colours) and by use of the fruits of the nature, flowers, etc.

07fa4973-f69d-57f4-8e6d-caeb88f75252.name: Belt with buckles
07fa4973-f69d-57f4-8e6d-caeb88f75252.dimensions: Belt: 88 x 7.5 cm, buckles: 27 x 12 cm
07fa4973-f69d-57f4-8e6d-caeb88f75252.author: Milena Petrovic, ethnologist
07fa4973-f69d-57f4-8e6d-caeb88f75252.materials: Cotton fabric, *srma* – silver and gold-wrapped thread, braids. Buckles: silver, hammering, decorative stones
07fa4973-f69d-57f4-8e6d-caeb88f75252.second_name: Articles of adornment worn at the waist – *pafti*
07fa4973-f69d-57f4-8e6d-caeb88f75252.description2: Buckles were the most prominent articles of adornment worn by Macedonian women. They were also the most frequently worn pieces of jewellery, having been an inevitable element of folk costumes in all parts of Macedonia. Combining functionality and aesthetics, buckles were also considered to play a protective role. The diverse shapes – round, rectangular, leaf-shaped, etc., as well as the exquisite style of their decorating, show the remarkable skill and talent of goldsmiths producing them. These buckles consist of two slightly concave round plates joined with a little round piece used for fastening. They are adorned with decorative stones and decorated with geometric patterns applied by hammering. The belt is made of cotton fabric decorated with geometric and floral patterns by application of silver and gold-wrapped thread and braids.

08c133b3-6259-5695-84a5-63de2f4fdb57.name: Victor Hugo at Casteret
08c133b3-6259-5695-84a5-63de2f4fdb57.description2: A number of important political and literary figures moved abroad during Napoléon III's authoritarian rule. This was the case with Victor Hugo, who left France between 1852 and 1870 as he refused to live under the reign of, "Napoléon le Petit", as he liked to call him.

0938866e-9a77-5d93-86b4-888bd58845d1.name: *Constantinople*
0938866e-9a77-5d93-86b4-888bd58845d1.description2: With the political developments of 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. Travelling in the 19th century became easier and more reliable due to the advent of steamships and trains. Westerners travelled to the East not only for touristic purposes, but also for scientific research, history, archaeology or for religious reasons. Western travellers told of their experiences and what they saw in eastern countries in their travel books and they even offer advice about the journey. Istanbul, where East and West meet, has been the subject of many a traveller's book.

0ba2e663-9318-562e-9c2a-099d167e8112.name: Earrings
0ba2e663-9318-562e-9c2a-099d167e8112.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
0ba2e663-9318-562e-9c2a-099d167e8112.author: Huda Kilani
0ba2e663-9318-562e-9c2a-099d167e8112.keywords: 23 karat gold; rosettes; coral; Ottoman coins
0ba2e663-9318-562e-9c2a-099d167e8112.description2: 23-karat gold earrings from South Palestine (Beer Sheba), with red stones, blue talismans mounted on rosettes of coral, and gold Ottoman coins (dated 1808). Silver jewellery was the most common because only rich people could afford gold jewellery. Silver or gold jewellery was part of the dowry given by the groom to the bride. The material (gold or silver) and even the coins used as pieces of jewellery were an indirect statement of the financial status of the groom.

0dd30a0a-1b26-5aa8-95ed-2abdad17a184.name: *Tercüman-ı Ahval* Newspaper
0dd30a0a-1b26-5aa8-95ed-2abdad17a184.description2: *Tercüman-ı Ahvâl* was the first private newspaper published in Istanbul. It was produced between 1860-1866 by Agah Efendi and Şinasi, men of letters of Tanzimat Era. Initially it was published only on Sundays, but starting from the 25th issue in 1861, it was published three times a week. Leading authors of the period such as Ahmed Vefik Paşa, Ziya Paşa and Refik Bey frequently wrote for it, discussing the reasons for the backwardness of Ottoman society and current events. In the paper, works of literature were also published. For instance the first Turkish theatre play, *Wedding/Marriage* of the Poet, by Şinasi (1860) was published as a series. The paper was closed for two weeks in 1861 after a very critical article probably written by Ziya Paşa. This is regarded as the first example of a ban in Turkish press. The paper was no longer published after 11 March 1866.

0dda7d39-b57f-5849-bcea-6897a0d0d4be.name: Amulet
0dda7d39-b57f-5849-bcea-6897a0d0d4be.author: Milena Petrovic, ethnologist
0dda7d39-b57f-5849-bcea-6897a0d0d4be.description2: Throughout the 19th century in Macedonia, jewellery was not used only for adornment; it also served an apotropaic function. People used to wear various kinds of reliquaries for the purpose of personal protection from evil spirits. These protective items used to be worn in pockets or sewn to the garment. This amulet is made of silver using the techniques of hammering and engraving. The rectangular plate depicts the Virgin and Child flanked by two angels above them. The rings on the sides show that the amulet must have been worn suspended on a chain.

0eb45a82-3f02-52db-8222-86625075ccdf.name: Bridal coat (*Klashenik*)
0eb45a82-3f02-52db-8222-86625075ccdf.author: Gordanche Vidinic, ethnologist
0eb45a82-3f02-52db-8222-86625075ccdf.keywords: klashenik; broad cloth; textile; embroidery; geometric patterns; geometric motifs; costume; wedding; marriage
0eb45a82-3f02-52db-8222-86625075ccdf.materials: Thick woollen fabric, twill-weave, embroidery with *srma* and decoration with wool braids
0eb45a82-3f02-52db-8222-86625075ccdf.description2: A *klashenik* is a kind of over-garment women used to wear in winter. It is split in the front and made of thick woollen broadcloth called *klashna*. This piece is long to the hips. It is adorned with red braids along the hems. It is also decorated with embroidery of geometric patterns on the sleeves and at the breasts. Every ethnic area in Macedonia had distinct style of traditional costume, yet all of them show undeniable influence of Oriental art.

0fb21836-e5e1-51dd-ab52-da180f9f90b6.name: Oud
0fb21836-e5e1-51dd-ab52-da180f9f90b6.holder: Lebanese National Higher Conservatory of Music
0fb21836-e5e1-51dd-ab52-da180f9f90b6.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Hassan El Masri, Remy Nader
0fb21836-e5e1-51dd-ab52-da180f9f90b6.description2: The oud is the Arabic word for a lute, a pear-shaped instrument with a short fretted kneck and six sets of double strings. It is played with a plectrum, usually made of trimmed eagle feather, and has a deep, mellow sound. The word 'lute' in English comes from the Arabic "al-oud", via the Spanish word for the instrument, "laúd".

109ed34a-507a-5652-bb30-736569eca0ac.name: Drum
109ed34a-507a-5652-bb30-736569eca0ac.holder: Jordan Folklore Museum, Department of Antiquities
109ed34a-507a-5652-bb30-736569eca0ac.author: Huda Kilani
109ed34a-507a-5652-bb30-736569eca0ac.keywords: drum; animals skin; linen rope; wooden stick; Ramadan; to wake up
109ed34a-507a-5652-bb30-736569eca0ac.description2: Small round drum, pointed on the bottom, covered on the top with leather, and fastened with a linen rope. It was played with a wooden stick to create special sounds of music, and it was used during the Muslim holy month of Ramadan to wake up people to eat (*suhur*) before sunrise. Some people used to volunteer to go around before dawn to wake people up during Holy Ramadan, reflecting community spirit.

11568132-d5af-54cf-9a3f-f663abfb4f5b.name: Winter jacket
11568132-d5af-54cf-9a3f-f663abfb4f5b.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
11568132-d5af-54cf-9a3f-f663abfb4f5b.author: Huda Kilani
11568132-d5af-54cf-9a3f-f663abfb4f5b.materials: Wool, cotton and silk; hand weaving and hand embroidered
11568132-d5af-54cf-9a3f-f663abfb4f5b.description2: Sleeveless jacket made of woollen fabric of red and black stripes, decorated with floral motifs of orange and purple colour with couching in silk threads on the shoulders and the bottom. This object illustrates the variegated population composition of the Jordanian territory in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, influenced by the local economy. The main activities were trade and crafts that influenced population movements and the coexistence of various local and foreign communities.

12ae0ba0-fa77-59bd-a23f-763b7a6f9512.name: Four anklets
12ae0ba0-fa77-59bd-a23f-763b7a6f9512.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
12ae0ba0-fa77-59bd-a23f-763b7a6f9512.description2: Ankle bracelets - or "anklets" - were common accessories in various regions of the ancient Middle East. They were first worn by ancient Egyptian women, and were made of materials such as brass, gold, silver, iron, glass, or ivory. The Hebrew word for "ankle chain" and "step chains" both come from the root *tsa'adh'*, meaning "to take steps; to march". The Hebrew word *e'khes*, meaning "bangle; anklet" comes from the root *akhas*, meaning "to make a tinkling sound" or "shaking bangles". Indeed, many anklets were adorned with small bells and heavier anklets would have made a loud tinkling or ringing noise as the wearer walked along. These bells were usually fashioned by placing a small pebble in hollowed silver spheres. It is possible that heavier anklets would have been designed to restrict the woman's step, thus forcing her to walk slowly in a style perceived as feminine, or to attract attention as she walked. The anklets pictured here are made of silver and are adorned with small dangling silver bells.

13caa9ac-5165-5334-9cdf-31b3219e01b9.name: *Sipahis of Algiers*
13caa9ac-5165-5334-9cdf-31b3219e01b9.archival: Berbrugger, *Algérie Historique Pittoresque et Monumentale*, Paris: J. Delahaye, 1843.

14d25094-56e3-5812-add7-3c7c717c6829.name: Mijwiz
14d25094-56e3-5812-add7-3c7c717c6829.holder: Lebanese National Higher Conservatory of Music
14d25094-56e3-5812-add7-3c7c717c6829.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Hassan El Masri, Remy Nader
14d25094-56e3-5812-add7-3c7c717c6829.description2: The *mijwiz*, meaning "double" in Arabic, is a common instrument in traditional Lebanese music. It is a type of reed clarinet, played by breathing slowly through a circular aperture at the end of the instrument, and covering the holes down the body of the instrument with your fingers in order to create different notes.

16c4b489-744b-54ba-b2f9-e9d429647ac5.name: Bracelet in French Egyptian Revival style
16c4b489-744b-54ba-b2f9-e9d429647ac5.author: Marina Minozzi
16c4b489-744b-54ba-b2f9-e9d429647ac5.keywords: Revivalism; Egyptomania; Egyptian motifs; applied arts; jewellery; exploration; archaeology; excavation; scientific expedition; Campaign in Egypt; Campaign in Syria; Enlightenment; science; technique; Egyptology; Orientalism; travel; botany; epigraphy
16c4b489-744b-54ba-b2f9-e9d429647ac5.description2: This bracelet, owned by Princess Paolina Bonaparte (1780–1825), wife of Camillo Borghese, was made by one of the most famous goldsmiths in Paris, Jean Baptiste Claude Odiot, as identified by the trademark on the safety lock of the bracelet. The elegant Egyptian decoration made by hieroglyphics and triangles alternating with little palms is inspired to the book *Voyage dans le Basse et Haute Égypte*, written by Dominique Vivant Denon (1745–1825) during Napoleon’s campaign along the Nile river in 1798 and published between 1802 and 1810. The ancient Egyptian fashion, popular in Italy since the second half of the 18th century, influenced furniture design and works of art following publication of Denon’s book, which popularized a “retour d’Egypte”.

en: Costamagna, A., *La raffinatezza e il lusso: lo "stile" Borghese dal cardinale Scipione ai principi Camillo e Paolina in quattro piccoli "tesori" artistici*, Rome: Galleria Borghese, 2005: 23–27.

178d2db5-fbc1-5e5a-8ce8-245dc22c7cea.name: Arabian *bisht*
178d2db5-fbc1-5e5a-8ce8-245dc22c7cea.description2: Arabian *bisht* made from black cloth and gold thread.

179f9d9d-6b5a-52fc-8dea-c159da198fd5.name: *La Reine de Saba: 14 costume sketches*
179f9d9d-6b5a-52fc-8dea-c159da198fd5.description2: Charles Gounod turned to the librettists Jules Barbier and Michel Carré for advice when he was writing his great opera, and so they recommended him the legend of Hiram, the great tale narrated by Gérard de Nervale in his *Voyage en Orient*. The opera was put on in Paris in 1862. As this costume from the court of Suleiman shows, the models and costumes responded above all to the Orientalist stereotypes in vogue at the time.

19f232dc-5ab5-59c1-9ebb-efa8da82d771.name: *Turkish woman at the hammam or baths*
19f232dc-5ab5-59c1-9ebb-efa8da82d771.keywords: costume; hammam; women; fashion; Orientalism; travel; traveller; Ottoman bath culture
19f232dc-5ab5-59c1-9ebb-efa8da82d771.description2: Sheet from *Costumes Turcs*, a lavish set of volumes produced in Turkey for a European audience. They present the appearance of people from different areas, with different jobs etc.

1bf2807f-b480-5653-a4f4-e5a1183a5629.name: Dura'ah coat
1bf2807f-b480-5653-a4f4-e5a1183a5629.keywords: costume; cotton; silk; silk trade; Syria
1bf2807f-b480-5653-a4f4-e5a1183a5629.description2: Druze, Galilee. Most of this coat, apart from the brown cotton sleeves, is made from luxury fabrics imported from Syria or Europe: red satin and panels of  blue and silver brocade, which are attached with large red running stitches. The cord edging shows Ottoman influence.

1ded3dd3-7a23-59f6-a90a-327c278ea1a9.name: Portrait of Shaykh Qasim al-Kusty
1ded3dd3-7a23-59f6-a90a-327c278ea1a9.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Hassan El Masri, Remy Nader
1ded3dd3-7a23-59f6-a90a-327c278ea1a9.description2: Shaykh Qasimal-Kusty was born in Beirut in 1840. He studied Arabic literature alongside great masters of his time, such as Shaykh Ibrahim al-Ahdab and Shaykh Yusuf al-Asir. He practiced teaching for a while, before publishing his first collection of poetry. He also assisted with theatrical productions. He died in 1909.

1f14a324-c1e9-5296-b0e9-2ac16800da16.name: Old wooden slippers
1f14a324-c1e9-5296-b0e9-2ac16800da16.description2: Slippers made out of wood that was usually worn for comfort.

1f2e44d5-854a-519d-868a-777ceb2535e3.name: *Les Folies Turques: quadrille*
1f2e44d5-854a-519d-868a-777ceb2535e3.description2: The 18th century fascination with "turkeries" was followed in the 19th century by a trend for music with more stereotypical, supposedly "oriental" motifs. This operetta about "turkish follies", is an example of this.

204ad655-e0e1-593a-b96e-0e6675438945.name: A Druse Bride from Lebanon
204ad655-e0e1-593a-b96e-0e6675438945.holder: National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography “Luigi Pigorini”
204ad655-e0e1-593a-b96e-0e6675438945.author: Vito Lattanzi, Marina Minozzi
204ad655-e0e1-593a-b96e-0e6675438945.keywords: Woman; photograph; anthropology; ethnology; geography; travel; exploration; scientific expedition; ethnography; museums; model; genre picture; portrait; representation of the other; costume; material culture; collection; Lebanon; Druze
204ad655-e0e1-593a-b96e-0e6675438945.description2: The bride wears a tantur, a head ornament worn along with a white veil by the women from Antilibano. The photo belonging to Enrico H. Giglioli's collection was collected by the Florentine naturalist on his world travels in 1865 to 1868 as he advanced diplomatic and commercial affairs between the newborn Italian state and the other nations. The images seem to have been created spontaneously to show ethnocentric diversity. The ethnographic photographs in the Giglioli's collection are part of the historical archive of the Pigorini Museum and are important for the histories of anthropological science and photography. The origins of scientific activity and conservation of Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico "Luigi Pigorini" in Rome can be traced back to the 1875 foundation of the "Royal National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography in Rome" within the buildings of the Roman College.

20742252-5d4f-565f-8b1e-0849b9510ddd.name: Abdul-Mejid I, Sultan of Turkey (1823–1861)
20742252-5d4f-565f-8b1e-0849b9510ddd.keywords: Abdul-Mejid, Sultan of Turkey; Egypt; Syria, Palestine; Hungarian refugees
20742252-5d4f-565f-8b1e-0849b9510ddd.description2: Portrait of Abdul-Mejid I, Sultan of Turkey (1823–1861). When he came to power in 1839, he tried to re-occupy lands lost to Muhammad 'Ali, the ruler of Egypt. In this effort he was supported by Britain and Austria. In 1840 a combined British-Austrian fleet cut off the supply lines of the Egyptian army and forced the Egyptians to sign the 1840 Convention of Alexandria. Abdul-Mejid was able to win back Syria and Palestine. In 1849 he granted the Hungarian refugees exile. In 1861 he died and left his throne to his brother Abdülaziz.

2183a68a-715b-5bb8-90dd-50fb40a8968f.name: Seventy-five necklaces
2183a68a-715b-5bb8-90dd-50fb40a8968f.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
2183a68a-715b-5bb8-90dd-50fb40a8968f.keywords: Decoration; Silver; Silver chains; Jewels; Semi-precious stones; Necklace
2183a68a-715b-5bb8-90dd-50fb40a8968f.description2: Seventy-five Ottoman-era silver necklaces decorated with multi-coloured semi-precious stones.

21d264d1-3d1b-5ec6-b7d4-e5b54eaaed68.name: *Bindallı entari*
21d264d1-3d1b-5ec6-b7d4-e5b54eaaed68.holder: Vehbi Koç Foundation Sadberk Hanim Museum
21d264d1-3d1b-5ec6-b7d4-e5b54eaaed68.dimensions: H (front): 128 c, h (back): 146 cm, sleeves: 49 cm
21d264d1-3d1b-5ec6-b7d4-e5b54eaaed68.description2: The attire of Ottoman women included dresses for the outdoors and the indoors. Starting from early 19th century, dresses called *üçetek* (dress with three skirts) and *dörtetek* (dress with four skirts) became fashionable. As relations with Europe increased, women in Istanbul started to use imported European textiles for their new dresses. This *entari* (dress) is made of purple velvet embroidered in the *bindallı* (dress that has embroidered flowers on the branches) style with garlands and flowers in vases in the *dival* (gold or silver embroidery on velvet) technique using silver-gilt thread. It has a short front opening, round neck and fitted sleeves. The skirt is widened by triangular gores and is longer at the back.

229ce446-298c-5552-9810-3b37da02fac9.name: *Tulumbacı*
229ce446-298c-5552-9810-3b37da02fac9.keywords: costume; Orientalism; travel; traveller; Ottoman army; Devşirme; Janissaries; court life; fashion; military wear
229ce446-298c-5552-9810-3b37da02fac9.description2: Sheet from *Costumes Turcs*, a lavish set of volumes produced in Turkey for a European audience. They present the appearance of people from different areas, with different jobs etc. *Tulumbacı*, a member of the Janissary fire brigade.

22b59916-1001-5666-873e-2d7a62f3d991.name: *Keswa kabbous (wedding outfit)*
22b59916-1001-5666-873e-2d7a62f3d991.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
22b59916-1001-5666-873e-2d7a62f3d991.keywords: Wedding outfit; embroidery with silver thread.
22b59916-1001-5666-873e-2d7a62f3d991.description2: Worn by the bride during the wedding ceremony, the keswa kabous el-Jaraq weighs more than ten kilograms. It consists of a large, billowing pair of trousers secured at the waist by a tekka (similar to a ribbon), with a matching top, short enough to leave the waist uncovered, both made of silk taffeta. Its air of great wealth and elegance comes particularly from the contrast between the floral motifs, embroidered with a flat silver thread, and the sequins, also sewn on with a gold and silver thread. When worn by a seated bride, the trousers resemble a large hoop-skirt, connected to a low-necked bodice, which together give the impression of being a robe de cour (grand habit). The upper section of these trousers, hemmed at the waist but open at the front, consists of almost four metres of fabric, and the legs alone have a circumference of one and a half metres and are a metre long. The end of the legs is hemmed with some robust percale fabric, which contains the hemming and rises up the leg to create an even larger swell around the ankle.

2398d928-c319-50b3-8b82-b2185dea28d6.name: *Lady Layard*
2398d928-c319-50b3-8b82-b2185dea28d6.keywords: Assyrian revival; women; archaeology; exploration; travel; traveller
2398d928-c319-50b3-8b82-b2185dea28d6.description2: Lady Layard, wife of the famous excavator of Assyria, Austen Henry Layard, here poses in ‘Assyrian’ jewellery. This was made for her using genuine ancient objects.

23e1371d-e17b-5b84-a037-47dc18e8eb2f.name: *Qittan*
23e1371d-e17b-5b84-a037-47dc18e8eb2f.description2: A very rare piece purchased from Sheikh Sa\`ud in 2002. This was his personal *thawb* and he said he found wearing it very relaxing. Called *qittan*, which means 'cord', the piece is embroidered around the neck up until the ends of sleeves, with silk thread. It also contains silk ball buttons.

23edfc09-0c9b-59bb-960f-61e8838f93b3.name: Shoes
23edfc09-0c9b-59bb-960f-61e8838f93b3.description: White and blue satin shoes. They are flat and have a sharply raised toecap. The sole is made of leather. The surface is partially covered in yellow silk; they are adorned with gold sequins and a yellow tassel.
23edfc09-0c9b-59bb-960f-61e8838f93b3.holder: Museum of Costume, Ethnographical Heritage Research Centre
23edfc09-0c9b-59bb-960f-61e8838f93b3.dimensions: Height 5 cm, Length 27,2 cm, Width 6,3 cm
23edfc09-0c9b-59bb-960f-61e8838f93b3.author: Elena Vázquez

26bb48d2-0468-5e95-b709-f3f74817bef6.name: Man's trousers (*Chakshiri*)
26bb48d2-0468-5e95-b709-f3f74817bef6.author: Gordanche Vidinic, ethnologist
26bb48d2-0468-5e95-b709-f3f74817bef6.description2: There used to be around fifty diverse styles of folk costumes worn in different ethnic areas throughout Macedonia in the 19th century and in the early 20th century. Among the most prominent were the costumes of Gorni Polog. Unlike the diverse and numerous women’s garments, men’s outfits were much simpler and rather unified. These men's trousers of white canvas are decorated plainly with black braids.

272aabb1-2d59-5faa-9ce5-a28c1305a906.name: Brass head of flagpole
272aabb1-2d59-5faa-9ce5-a28c1305a906.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
272aabb1-2d59-5faa-9ce5-a28c1305a906.author: Huda Kilani
272aabb1-2d59-5faa-9ce5-a28c1305a906.description2: This mast, made of casted brass, bears an Arabic calligraphic decoration with the inscription "Oh God, Oh Muhammad". It is fixed on a pointed piece of copper with a hole at the bottom to install on a long wooden staff. In religious festivities such as pilgrimage, various activities were organized. They would normally include festivals and rallies under flags and standards. The heads of flagstaffs were decorated with metallic items usually with Arabic calligraphy and some cosmic signs such as the crescent and the star.

2739eecb-f1a1-5544-8ead-dcf31ff17148.name: An elderly Paul Draneht (1815–94) with his daughter Despina
2739eecb-f1a1-5544-8ead-dcf31ff17148.author: Massimiliano Cremona, Ignazio Galella
2739eecb-f1a1-5544-8ead-dcf31ff17148.description2: In 1894, Paul Draneht, who had been awarded the title of Pasha, died in Alexandria. His daughter Despina married a Greek businessman, Emmanuel Zervudachi, and the family continued to be part of a Mediterranean cosmopolitan elite.

2750ade6-0ba3-536b-a712-3d37388d9bf1.name: *Nuit d'Orient*. \[waltz for piano, op. 11\]
2750ade6-0ba3-536b-a712-3d37388d9bf1.artist: Illustrator: Léonce Burret; composer: P. Bermalty
2750ade6-0ba3-536b-a712-3d37388d9bf1.description2: Musical composers' fascination with the "Orient" manifested itself in their music and their titles. The "harem" had intrigued Westerners for a long time.

279e1f50-df40-5f44-a5e0-e9a46ddf29b7.name: Bridal coat (*Klashenik*)
279e1f50-df40-5f44-a5e0-e9a46ddf29b7.author: Gordanche Vidinic, ethnologist
279e1f50-df40-5f44-a5e0-e9a46ddf29b7.keywords: klashenik; broad cloth; textile; embroidery; costume; wedding; marriage
279e1f50-df40-5f44-a5e0-e9a46ddf29b7.materials: Thick twill-weave woollen fabric decorated with braids
279e1f50-df40-5f44-a5e0-e9a46ddf29b7.description2: A *klashenik* is a kind of over-garment in varying lengths and split on the front made of thick woollen broadcloth called *klashna*. This knee-length piece comes from the Veles Region. It is abundantly adorned with embroidery above the lower hem and at the breasts. Embroidery was an inevitable part of decorating the majority of Macedonian folk costumes. The exquisite, meticulously executed embroidery applied on this tunic makes it a real work of art.

2820044b-9046-518a-901e-821f3cb8b715.name: Arabian gold dagger
2820044b-9046-518a-901e-821f3cb8b715.keywords: Weaponry; dagger; Arabian; Arab; floral decoration; weapon; arms; armours; costume; accessories; fashion; dance
2820044b-9046-518a-901e-821f3cb8b715.description2: Arabian (Omani) dagger belonging to Sheikh Abdullah bin Jassim. The dagger sheath is made of leather and embroidered with golden thread. The top and base of the sheath is decorated with a traditional flower design whilst the middle of the sheath is decorated with a leaf pattern. The dagger handle is made of rhinoceros ivory and is decorated with ten pearls. The dagger blade is steel called ‘*al-jawhar*’ which is derived from the finest Arabian Damascus plate.

2c003611-f7ea-5e9d-9992-13b824dcddc9.name: Portrait Khalil al-Khury
2c003611-f7ea-5e9d-9992-13b824dcddc9.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Hassan El Masri, Remy Nader
2c003611-f7ea-5e9d-9992-13b824dcddc9.description2: Khalil al-Khuri was born in Choiefat ('Aley) in October 1836. He founded the first non-official newspaper in Arabic, *Hadiqat al-Akhbar* (the garden of news) in 1858. He also wrote a collection of poems, some of which were later translated into French. He died in October, 1907.

2d85c81f-8fff-5170-9719-df9f41dbd763.name: Socks (*Chorapi*)
2d85c81f-8fff-5170-9719-df9f41dbd763.author: Gordanche Vidinic, ethnologist
2d85c81f-8fff-5170-9719-df9f41dbd763.keywords: home-made attire; knitting; silver; gold; embroidery; floral decoration; costume
2d85c81f-8fff-5170-9719-df9f41dbd763.materials: Knitted of wool and silver and gold-wrapped threads. Decoration with embroidery of varied wool
2d85c81f-8fff-5170-9719-df9f41dbd763.description2: In the 18th, 19th and early 20th centuries, all garments for the entire family were made by women themselves. They used to weave all the fabrics, except for the broadcloth, as well as to cut and sew the clothes, decorate them by embroidery and apply varied ornaments for embellishing. Women also used to knit the socks to match the outfit. These men’s socks belong to the set of traditional men’s costume from the Gorni Polog area. They are knitted from black wool and *srma* (silver and gold-wrapped threads). They have been additionally decorated with embroidered floral patterns in different colours.

2e2c6f60-7eec-5d13-9b2d-03e45b5cd72a.name: *Burqu\` rayyasi*
2e2c6f60-7eec-5d13-9b2d-03e45b5cd72a.description2: Face mask (also known in Arabic as *batula*) decorated with small embossed gold discs all around the forehead and sides. There are two matching gold clasps on each side of the forehead.

2e69a533-f8e1-5f1a-92fc-fc2a6fbcefa3.name: Portrait of Shaykh Ahmar Hasan Tabbara
2e69a533-f8e1-5f1a-92fc-fc2a6fbcefa3.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Hassan El Masri, Remy Nader
2e69a533-f8e1-5f1a-92fc-fc2a6fbcefa3.keywords: Writer; Symbol; Revolution; Books; Literature; Prison
2e69a533-f8e1-5f1a-92fc-fc2a6fbcefa3.description2: Shaykh Ahmar Hasan Tabbara was born in Beirut in 1870. He began writing and publishing in newspapers, such as *Thamarat al-Funun* at a young age. He later was an editor for the *al-Ittihad al-Usmani* newspaper. He was emprisoned during the First World War, and then hung alongside other Lebanese prisoners of war on 6 May 1916. He published a number of books in his lifetime, including an important manuscript of *Kalila wa Dimna*.

2f953756-84c0-5583-addd-4a04b14f482f.name: Shirt
2f953756-84c0-5583-addd-4a04b14f482f.description: White linen shirt, long and flared sleeves ruffled long fist, also shirred boat neckline and wedge in the armpits and on the skirt. On the neckline, sleeves and cuffs, bands embroidered with black wool based geometric, vegetable and rampant lions.

30b8ffa8-c9e2-5376-85c7-4955c327cf33.name: Bracelet
30b8ffa8-c9e2-5376-85c7-4955c327cf33.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
30b8ffa8-c9e2-5376-85c7-4955c327cf33.author: Huda Kilani
30b8ffa8-c9e2-5376-85c7-4955c327cf33.description2: Niello made by a Circassian silver smith. Mounted with an oval-shaped piece, with locking mechanism, decorated with niello decoration. The immigration of the Circassians to the Eastern Arab countries (they have spiritual and religious links with these countries) started in the middle of 19th century and continued until 1900.

30f458b3-4363-5cf5-82c6-91c5e3c06c7e.name: *Medjmouaï teçavir* (Collection de costumes)
30f458b3-4363-5cf5-82c6-91c5e3c06c7e.keywords: costume; fashion; military wear; court life; Ottoman imperial symbols; travel; traveller; Orientalism
30f458b3-4363-5cf5-82c6-91c5e3c06c7e.description2: Postcard from Turkey showing the costume worn by various people, according to occupation, activity, etc. Intended for a relatively popular western market. Illustrates the social structures and costumes of the last days of the Ottoman empire. Great reformer Mahmud II in European-influenced dress.

31b5f52e-c220-58fe-a02b-2b22d317bc2b.name: *Description of the Arab monuments of Granada, Seville and Córdoba: the Alhambra, the Alcazar and the Great Mosque*
31b5f52e-c220-58fe-a02b-2b22d317bc2b.description: The publications about the Spanish Muslim Antiquities, including monuments can be retraced to the end of the 18th century. Interest in these monuments is related to the interest in this unique heritage in Europe, as part of the Alhambresque and Neo-Mudéjar styles in Spain and Europe. The publication of the monument’s descriptions aided in their conservation.
31b5f52e-c220-58fe-a02b-2b22d317bc2b.author: Ana Cabrera
31b5f52e-c220-58fe-a02b-2b22d317bc2b.third_name: *Estudio descriptivo de los monumentos árabes de Granada, Sevilla y Córdoba o sea, La Alhambra, El Alcazar y la gran Mezquita de Occidente*

3385951b-c80c-5d8e-8659-f32b8e5ee6a7.name: Bridal coat
3385951b-c80c-5d8e-8659-f32b8e5ee6a7.author: Gordanche Vidinic, ethnologist
3385951b-c80c-5d8e-8659-f32b8e5ee6a7.keywords: upper garment; broad cloth; costume; textile; accessories; wedding; marriage
3385951b-c80c-5d8e-8659-f32b8e5ee6a7.materials: Klashna – thick woollen fabric adorned with balze, silver and gold-wrapped thread, silver string, sequins, beads and pompons of wool
3385951b-c80c-5d8e-8659-f32b8e5ee6a7.description2: Analysis of the evolution path of traditional costumes in the Republic of Macedonia have shown apparent influences of the Old Slav, Old Balkan, Byzantine and Turkish-Oriental cultures. This piece of traditional overcoat is an exquisite example of the application of *srma* – gold and silver-wrapped thread used widely in the Oriental handicraft of decorating garments. A *gornik* is a sleeveless upper garment made of white broadcloth called *klashna*. It has false sleeves hanging on the back. They are actually strips of white broadcloth richly adorned with pompoms of fluffy red wool, silver thread braids, a silver twisted ribbon, red baize, a silver string, sequins and beads. The lower part of the back is decorated in the same manner. Its rims and seams are also decorated with red and black braids.

339661cd-4f3b-50e8-ac7b-98082ee3d45c.name: *The mule which carries the Qur’an to Mecca*
339661cd-4f3b-50e8-ac7b-98082ee3d45c.keywords: costume; Qur'an; Orientalism; travel; traveller; hajj; pilgrimage; Hijaz; Ka'ba
339661cd-4f3b-50e8-ac7b-98082ee3d45c.description2: Sheet from *Costumes Turcs*, a lavish set of volumes produced in Turkey for a European audience. They present the appearance of people from different areas, with different jobs etc.

3583d624-13fa-58e9-9d82-9ef1b2d476f5.name: *Beethoven at the Palace*
3583d624-13fa-58e9-9d82-9ef1b2d476f5.holder: Mimar Sinan Fine Arts University, Painting and Sculpture Museum
3583d624-13fa-58e9-9d82-9ef1b2d476f5.description2: Caliph Abdulmecid was interested in art in addition to administration. He opened many art exhibitions. He was chosen as honorary president of the Society of Ottoman Painters, which was founded in 1909, and he gave considerable financial support to the monthly journal published by the society. He took part in the Galatasaray Art Exhibitions with his paintings. For example, one of his paintings was accepted for an exhibition held at Galatasaray during the first years of the First World War. His works reveal him as a colourist and an accomplished portrait painter. Caliph Abdulmecid showed his paintings at the Viyana Exhibition, which was the first exhibition opened by Turkish painters in Europe in 1918.

3a20e143-6e36-5c47-8630-b7694a01419b.name: Jubbeh
3a20e143-6e36-5c47-8630-b7694a01419b.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Hassan El Masri, Remy Nader
3a20e143-6e36-5c47-8630-b7694a01419b.materials: The original was made of cotton and satin
3a20e143-6e36-5c47-8630-b7694a01419b.second_name: Villager from the Beqaa Valley in traditional dress

3a2530bf-22b3-5651-bacc-f8a748c678a1.name: Headdress
3a2530bf-22b3-5651-bacc-f8a748c678a1.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
3a2530bf-22b3-5651-bacc-f8a748c678a1.author: Huda Kilani
3a2530bf-22b3-5651-bacc-f8a748c678a1.keywords: cotton; embroidered; gold coins; Ottoman coins
3a2530bf-22b3-5651-bacc-f8a748c678a1.materials: Gold, silver, cotton fabric, silk; casting; hand embroidered
3a2530bf-22b3-5651-bacc-f8a748c678a1.description2: A rectangular piece of cotton cloth embroidered with cross-stitching forming a bonnet with a line of 70 gold coins (*ghawasi*) sewn together on the front, with two pieces of cloth on the top sides with silver Ottoman coins and red stuffed velvet pursed from the back side with 7 silver Ottoman coins. The silver coins were used as money and as jewellery given by the groom to the bride, thus being an indication of his financial status. This object reflects the variegated population composition of Jordan in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. It illustrates common elements and traditions in the area in fashion, costumes and social rites. There were no political boundaries at that period between the Jordanian and Palestinians territories. Some cities were like twins because of their close proximity and the exchange of trade goods and business.

3a359947-9b29-545c-9931-7f7be38d3ff5.name: Bracelet
3a359947-9b29-545c-9931-7f7be38d3ff5.description: This bracelet is made from engraved silver was made in 19th century Lebanon.
3a359947-9b29-545c-9931-7f7be38d3ff5.author: Marie Therese Moujabber

3ab9503a-ce96-572b-920f-f71d81fadf1c.name: Jacket
3ab9503a-ce96-572b-920f-f71d81fadf1c.holder: Musée Public National des Arts et Traditions Populaires
3ab9503a-ce96-572b-920f-f71d81fadf1c.description2: This small circumcision jacket from old Algiers is made of velvet from Gênes. It is decorated with a palm-leaf pattern and an acorn hanging between each pair of leaves. The sleeves and the edges of the jacket are decorated with a criss-cross pattern.

3bc9a9b0-a7fe-59d9-9819-5e3a9265f4a4.name: Egyptianising necklace
3bc9a9b0-a7fe-59d9-9819-5e3a9265f4a4.description2: Gold fringe necklace in the  form of cast alternating lotus flowers and buds. Illustrates the influence of Egyptian motifs on 19th French jewellery. As was typical, this necklace is not derived from an original, but a more free creation based on patrern books.

3cd5a4c9-7c30-53cb-877b-5bf9e71bca5b.name: *One Thousand and One Nights: Arabic fairytales tanslated by Galland, illustrated by the best French artists…*
3cd5a4c9-7c30-53cb-877b-5bf9e71bca5b.second_name: *This edition of the One Thousand and One Nights is a beautiful new volume of eleven hundred and twenty pages* \[…\] *subscriptions available in all bookshops: published in 52 installments.*
3cd5a4c9-7c30-53cb-877b-5bf9e71bca5b.description2: The *One Thousand and One Nights* played an important role in bringing the East and the West closer together. Galland was its first French translator, translating with much liberty the tales that he had been able to understand in the early 18th century. The translated One Thousand and One Nights were extremely successful, and became the subject of a variety of art forms, both allowing Europeans to become better acquainted with the Arab world, but also forming the basis for lasting stereotypes.

3e51e99d-8ff0-545e-95fc-52a15be8b042.name: *A Coffee House in Tophane*
3e51e99d-8ff0-545e-95fc-52a15be8b042.archival: Orientalist Paintings Collection-Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation Collection
3e51e99d-8ff0-545e-95fc-52a15be8b042.keywords: Thomas Allom; Jivanian; Orientalism; painting; İstanbul
3e51e99d-8ff0-545e-95fc-52a15be8b042.description2: A Thomas Allom composition which appears in the first volume of Robert Walsh’s book *Constantinople and Scenery of Seven Churches of Asia Minor* is *The Coffee-House*. This is an oil copy of the composition by Civanyan. Written by Robert Walsh, who served as the private priest of British ambassador Lord Strangford after 1820, the book was published in two volumes in London in 1838. It includes engravings and the book, which was later published in French, acted as an important visual resource on Istanbul and its engravings were used as models by numerous artists. In the corresponding text, Robert Walsh provides information on the interior organisation and decoration of the coffeehouse and relates various details ranging from making music and smoking pipes to the plays of the *meddah* (storytellers).

3f21696b-6178-5310-a618-3b1cbb1ec3d6.name: *Shéhérazade*
3f21696b-6178-5310-a618-3b1cbb1ec3d6.description2: George Auriol, the typographer renamed after his creations, was a multitalented artist, and thus in his work he reflected many different influences of the late 19th century. As an artist and musician, he was interested in the different graphic movements, as is clear from this image: the theme is clearly "Oriental", but the composition of the piece borrows characteristics from Japanese aesthetics and Art Nouveau.

40cc028f-a362-5724-b6be-dad14e9c2277.name: *Dagla zabun*
40cc028f-a362-5724-b6be-dad14e9c2277.materials: Cream twill, weave wool fabric, polychrome wool, embroidery threads, brown cotton knit braid, knotted brown silk buttons.
40cc028f-a362-5724-b6be-dad14e9c2277.description2: Men’s ceremonial coat style gown. Full-length A-line coat made from fine cream wool that was embroidered prior to being cut. It is likely that the coat was made from embroidered Kashmiri shawls decorated on corners and edges. Materials are cream twill, weave wool fabric, polychrome wool, embroidery threads, brown cotton knit braid, and 2 knotted brown silk buttons. This type of un-dyed wool is very fine, and we have only one. When this type of coat came back in to popularity, this specific design and color never appeared again. It is very rare. Lined with un-dyed silk in a natural color. There is a slit on the side for a pocket.

4160c0f6-fb41-5587-96d2-e482623adff8.name: Shoes
4160c0f6-fb41-5587-96d2-e482623adff8.description: Purple velvet flat slippers, with leather soles in their natural colour lined with blue leather. The blade is decorated with floral and geometric motifs in enhancement embroidery of gold metallic thread.

42b5c7f1-cc74-5b88-8ab4-25e33352b53f.name: Gilet
42b5c7f1-cc74-5b88-8ab4-25e33352b53f.holder: Musée Public National des Arts et Traditions Populaires
42b5c7f1-cc74-5b88-8ab4-25e33352b53f.description2: This bodice (*frimla*) was worn by young Algerian women. The back is decorated with an interlaced pattern, emerging from a stylised vase. Young Muslim and Jewish girls wore this gilet.

44156a31-6bfc-5a44-9e81-6e02ec39aee7.name: Jacket
44156a31-6bfc-5a44-9e81-6e02ec39aee7.holder: Musée Public National des Arts et Traditions Populaires
44156a31-6bfc-5a44-9e81-6e02ec39aee7.description2: This short men's jacket is embroidered on the two front panels, with a decoration consisting of curls, all ending in a hook shape and bordered by a floral motif emerging from a stylised vase. The open, elbow-length sleeves are decorated with geometric motifs. The sleeves are secured by small, mother-of-pearl buttons. This formal jacket was worn for important ceremonies.

45aa6bbe-dbdf-5f6e-b23b-222901c8201e.description2: This a music instrument developed in the early 20th century and used for folk dances played at engagements, weddings and other traditional celebrations.

485d12ca-7825-5990-8b96-58cf495684ae.name: *Drummer*
485d12ca-7825-5990-8b96-58cf495684ae.keywords: costume; music; Ottoman musical instruments; fashion; court life; travel; traveller; Orientalism; Ottoman army; Janissaries; Devşirme
485d12ca-7825-5990-8b96-58cf495684ae.description2: Sheet from a lavish set of volumes produced in Turkey for a European audience. They present the appearance of people from different areas, with different jobs etc. *Köşcü*, the drummer who played the big drum (*köş*) in the Mehter band.

48a64aba-b279-5473-911b-51ced2c8a938.name: Portrait Album – Ottoman State Officers
48a64aba-b279-5473-911b-51ced2c8a938.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
48a64aba-b279-5473-911b-51ced2c8a938.dates: Late 19th century – beginning of the 20th century
48a64aba-b279-5473-911b-51ced2c8a938.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph Ancient Istanbul; Pascal Sebah
48a64aba-b279-5473-911b-51ced2c8a938.description2: With the political developments of the 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. As a result, close to 160 artists visited Istanbul in the 19th century. Pascal Sébah (1823-86) was a pioneer photographer who worked in Istanbul. Sébah opened a photography studio known as "El Chark " in Pera in 1857. The studio's most successful period started with the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873. Sébah formed a partnership with Joaillier Polycarpe in 1885. In 1899, the two partners bought Abdullah Frères's archives. For the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873, Pascal Sébah prepared *The Ottoman Clothing Album* to be exhibited at the Ottoman Stand.

4910bd38-cc21-5b54-81dc-f3e7ee09ef0a.name: Qaftan

4910bd38-cc21-5b54-81dc-f3e7ee09ef0a.description2: The lavish garments previously worn by Lebanese emirs and *shaykhs* were swapped in the 19th century for more sombre items, such as this Qaftan.

4b1cc99c-bdcc-51e9-bf03-770c80101277.name: Men's coat (*Mintan*)
4b1cc99c-bdcc-51e9-bf03-770c80101277.author: Gordanche Vidinic, ethnologist
4b1cc99c-bdcc-51e9-bf03-770c80101277.description2: There used to be around fifty diverse styles of folk costumes worn in different ethnic areas throughout Macedonia in the 19th century and in the early 20th century. Among the most prominent were the costumes of Gorni Polog. Unlike the diverse and numerous women’s garments, men’s outfits were much simpler and rather unified. This upper garment called a *mintan* is of plain cut. It is made of silk in a striped pattern. Its only decorations are pieces of black cloth applied to the sleeves.
