a508bec6-1ea4-51c9-b5d8-a70ddc2a7baf.description2: Musical composers' fascination with the "Orient" manifested itself in their music and their titles. The sphinx, for example, was a recurring symbol of "Egyptomania".

a57ada78-0cee-53e5-9161-c701a353df82.name: *The Coffee Shop*
a57ada78-0cee-53e5-9161-c701a353df82.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
a57ada78-0cee-53e5-9161-c701a353df82.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
a57ada78-0cee-53e5-9161-c701a353df82.description2: Coffee shops in the Near and Middle East were regular meeting places for men, who could while away hours chatting, playing domino, smoking and – crucially if dangerously – talking politics. In early 20th century Cairo as elsewhere, spedific cafes became important hubs for social and political discourse.This painting shows a traditional Near Eastern street café. Customers are sitting on long benches in front of its wooden openwork facade, A waiter with a red fez carries a brass coffee pot (dallah) and a tray. Behind him, through the wooden screen, the preparation area, in which the coffee is made, can just be seen on the left. A man wearing a white turban and blue gown, perhaps the proprietor, looks out on the right. All present are captivated by a carpet seller, who is standing in front of the cafe, offering up his wares.

a69264a8-566e-5e69-9661-65f4191695c9.name: Gold-embroidered, velvet Waistcoat
a69264a8-566e-5e69-9661-65f4191695c9.holder: Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilisation / Sharjah Museums Department
a69264a8-566e-5e69-9661-65f4191695c9.dates: Hegira late 13th – early 14th century / AD late 19th – early 20th century
a69264a8-566e-5e69-9661-65f4191695c9.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
a69264a8-566e-5e69-9661-65f4191695c9.description2: In the context of rising nationalisms, traditional costume played an important role, both in Europe and – to a lesser extent – in the Middle East.This long waistcoat is made of purple velvet with printed cotton lining. It carries extensive embroidery executed in gold-coloured metal thread, highlighting in particular the collar, the edges of the garment and the side pockets. Further ornamentation enhances the back. In the context of rising nationalisms, traditional costume played an important role, both in Europe and – to a lesser extent – in the Middle East. This waist coat may originally have been made in one of the European provinces of the Ottoman Empire, as it shows certain similarities with costume from the Balkans.

a91be56f-fdaa-598c-a438-db2d0512a2e7.name: *Athenian Bride*
a91be56f-fdaa-598c-a438-db2d0512a2e7.author: Tsigakou, The Rediscovery of Greece, p.191
a91be56f-fdaa-598c-a438-db2d0512a2e7.description2: Louis Dupré (1789–1837) visited Greece in 1819. He exhibited Greek subjects at the Salons of 1827, 1831, 1833 and 1855. In 1825 he published a set of colored lithographs of views and studies of costumes from Greece, entitled *Voyages à Athènes et Constantinople*. Dupré recorded his experiences of travel in the Levant in 1819 mainly through portraits of the people he met. In addition to the lithographs in this book, Dupré also produced loose broadsheet lithographed plates. Many of these are in the possession of the Cabinet des Estampes of the Bibliothèque Nationale. Much has been written on Dupré. *Athenian Bride* depicts the preparations of an Athenian wedding. The bride patiently waits as the groom is ritually shaved.

a9495bdc-29e8-5ac4-be85-88883d1f30cd.name: *Madame Josephine the Landlady of the Hotel Constantinople in a Turkish Dress*

a95b3b6a-66a7-5a79-99bd-6be598fec282.name: Dolmabahçe Palace Theatre under construction
a95b3b6a-66a7-5a79-99bd-6be598fec282.author: Bahattin Öztuncay
a95b3b6a-66a7-5a79-99bd-6be598fec282.description2: James Robertson came to Istanbul in 1841 to assist with modernization of the Imperial Mint and remained for 40 years, during which he served without interruption under no less than four Ottoman sultans. He started as head etcher in the Ottoman Mint. Then he began to take photos of Istanbul. He also painted watercolours, and in the early 1850s became interested in photography and went on to become a leading name among early photographers. Robertson’s Istanbul photographs are concerned primarily with the city’s historical monuments. They reveal the city’s magnificent Byzantine and Ottoman structures from different angles and with close-ups taken in an approach that is usually quite aesthetic. In this photo, Dolmabahçe Palace Theatre is seen under construction.

ad65725a-43b5-5119-ab17-edebfab3d1ae.name: Tantura
ad65725a-43b5-5119-ab17-edebfab3d1ae.description2: Woman's head-dress found on Mount Lebanon. Associated with the Druze. This type of headdress disappeared between 1860 and 1880 following changes in the Mount Lebanon political structure with the stronger centralisation of the Ottoman government.

ae42a45e-443f-5a1d-aaab-85cd72bce06d.name: *A Greek Mountaineer*
ae42a45e-443f-5a1d-aaab-85cd72bce06d.author: Washington, D.C., 1991, 80-81, no 28
ae42a45e-443f-5a1d-aaab-85cd72bce06d.description2: During the Ottoman occupation, Greek peasants who were dispossessed of their property often retreated to impregnable mountain regions, where they engaged in resistance against the Turks. These mountaineers, who both fascinated and frightened European travellers, were romanticised by artists and poets such as Lord Byron. The man depicted here clearly represents the type of mountaineer described by Byron. To emphasize his costume and his swift movement, he appears in full gear, the sleeves of his jacket falling freely to the back as if to underscore his impulsive gesture. Pistols and knives are tucked in his belt. His right hand rests on his musket; his left hand proudly touches the tip of his sword. Haag chose to place the figure in a grand mountainous landscape, complete with a ruined temple. This sacred monument may be identified as the temple of Apollo Epicurius in Arcadia in the central Peloponnese. This enhances the dignity of the figure, whose nobility and heroism are worthy of the principles of his legendary ancestors.

aef7807d-0cef-5b06-ba3e-6be4aa40ba9c.name: Turkish woman
aef7807d-0cef-5b06-ba3e-6be4aa40ba9c.description2: The Zangaki brothers were a pair of photographers working in Egypt who sold "Orientalist" photos to Western tourists, allowing them to immortalise their trip to the "Orient". This photograph shows a young Turkish woman.

af7e1b24-5d7e-5856-900a-6365e01610ba.name: Portrait Album – Ottoman State Officers
af7e1b24-5d7e-5856-900a-6365e01610ba.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
af7e1b24-5d7e-5856-900a-6365e01610ba.dates: Late 19th century – beginning of the 20th century
af7e1b24-5d7e-5856-900a-6365e01610ba.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph Ancient Istanbul; Pascal Sebah
af7e1b24-5d7e-5856-900a-6365e01610ba.description2: With the political developments of the 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. As a result, close to 160 artists visited Istanbul in the 19th century. Pascal Sébah (1823-86) was a pioneer photographer who worked in Istanbul. Sébah opened a photography studio known as "El Chark " in Pera in 1857. The studio's most successful period started with the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873. Sébah formed a partnership with Joaillier Polycarpe in 1885. In 1899, the two partners bought Abdullah Frères's archives. For the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873, Pascal Sébah prepared *The Ottoman Clothing Album* to be exhibited at the Ottoman Stand.

afe3b20f-d59e-5494-b4ec-e5a4b9544ad9.name: Zeybek Folk Dance
afe3b20f-d59e-5494-b4ec-e5a4b9544ad9.description2: Zeybek is a folk dance from Western Anatolia. It is done either by one or several dancers moving in a circle. Zeybek represents the protector. The dancer keeps his arms upright on the shoulder level while sometimes they are curled from elbow. He moves slowly with long steps. From time to time he kneels to touch his knee down.

b01b920c-bd76-5e6a-b3c9-4e331c550bdd.name: Karagöz and Hacivat Shadow Play
b01b920c-bd76-5e6a-b3c9-4e331c550bdd.description2: Shadow play consists of solid figures being shown and moved behind a semi-transparent screen. The characters of Hacivat and Karagöz plays reflect the multi-ethnic makeup of the Ottoman Empire. They are represented with a high level of detail through their figures, attitudes, dances, etc. Shadow play received its basic character in the 17th century and developed further in the following centuries, eventually becoming one of the most popular traditional forms of entertainment among Turks. It was performed by a single artist that is called a *hayali* (imaginary person) or *hayalbaz*. One of the main characteristics of shadow play is that the *hayali* changes his voice and manner of speaking depending on the character he was animating.

b25ced0a-8fbc-5812-85b3-eb1df7ad87a4.name: An Entertainment Scene (The third day of entertainment) from *Surname-i Vehbi*
b25ced0a-8fbc-5812-85b3-eb1df7ad87a4.archival: The Library of Sultan Ahmed III
b25ced0a-8fbc-5812-85b3-eb1df7ad87a4.description2: The image at the left shows an earlier stage of the flotilla. A long raft in the foreground carries a huge structure shaped like a cypress tree from which strings of fireworks are suspended along with two Catherine wheels. Rockets and projectiles hurtle about. On the basis of Vehbi’s account, this is the float prepared by the artillerymen’s corps. A two-story structure set on a pair of caiques carries a troupe of dancers and musicians on the lower floor while pyrotechnicists are busy at work on the upper one.

b54a4c02-3027-5de2-965f-2bb5a2395c13.name: Folk costume
b54a4c02-3027-5de2-965f-2bb5a2395c13.author: Nada Andonovska
b54a4c02-3027-5de2-965f-2bb5a2395c13.keywords: Embroidery; apron; Albanians; costume; floral decoration; geometric patterns; geometric decoration; geometric motifs
b54a4c02-3027-5de2-965f-2bb5a2395c13.materials: White canvas, embroidery, woollen home-woven fabric
b54a4c02-3027-5de2-965f-2bb5a2395c13.second_name: Traditional attire worn by Albanian women
b54a4c02-3027-5de2-965f-2bb5a2395c13.description2: The Albanian community is an important element in the multicultural milieu of ethnicities in the Republic of Macedonia. This outfit preserves some distinctive features of the clothing and adornment worn by Albanian women in Macedonia in the 19th century and early 20th century. The cotton canvas tunic is moderately decorated by embroidery of floral patterns on the sleeves and at the front part of the cleavage. The wool apron is embellished with geometric patterns woven of varied wool threads along the left and right hem, which end with woollen fringes in different colours.

b5c715a1-ea35-53d0-8de0-8e0d78cbb7d3.name: *Kurds charging, with Kettle-drummers leading*, from the book *Glimpses of Life and Manners in Persia*
b5c715a1-ea35-53d0-8de0-8e0d78cbb7d3.description:
Mary Leonor Woulfe Sheil, wife of Sir Justin Sheil, a British diplomat at the Qajar court in Persia (Iran), recorded in this book events from her journey to and life in Persia, from 7 August 1849 until June 1853. Persia was a strategic territory. Two years before Lady Shail's journey, a treaty redefined the frontiers between the Ottoman empire and the Qajar territories.  
  
The book describes people seen during the journey, court life, fashion, society, geography and the ancient irrigation system of the *qanat*s. Some of the events described reveal a hidden side of Persia – social unrest, in the shape of ideas considered by the author as a mixture of religious creed, socialism and communism: Lady Sheil witnessed the execution of the religious leader of the “Baabi” group, Sayyid Ali Mohammed, in Tabriz (1850).
b5c715a1-ea35-53d0-8de0-8e0d78cbb7d3.author: Maria Francesca Carvelli (MWNF)
b5c715a1-ea35-53d0-8de0-8e0d78cbb7d3.artist: Author of the book: Lady Mary Leonora Woulfe Sheil
b5c715a1-ea35-53d0-8de0-8e0d78cbb7d3.keywords: Women; travel; traveller; book; Iran; Persia; Qajar; treaty of Erzurum; Nasir al-Din Shah; railway; Constantinople; Bahaism; Bab; Sayyid 'Ali Muhammad al-Shirazi

b6227f02-1142-5b04-b3af-734ad8573ce6.name: Drums
b6227f02-1142-5b04-b3af-734ad8573ce6.holder: National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography “Luigi Pigorini”
b6227f02-1142-5b04-b3af-734ad8573ce6.dimensions: Upper diameter 12 cm; lower diameter 10 cm; height 28 cm
b6227f02-1142-5b04-b3af-734ad8573ce6.author: Vito Lattanzi, Marina Minozzi
b6227f02-1142-5b04-b3af-734ad8573ce6.keywords: Darbuka; ceramic; enamelling; cobalt-blue; bleau de Fez; Morocco; museums; collection; collector; anthropology; ethnology; travel; exploration; scientific expedition; geography; representation of the other; material culture; music; musical instrument
b6227f02-1142-5b04-b3af-734ad8573ce6.description2: The two drums are part of the flourishing tradition of enamelled ceramic in Fez, in production since the Middle Ages. Cobalt blue and white decorations identify Fez products dating to the second half of the 19th century. The drums belong to the ethnographic collections of the Pigorini Museum founded between the 19th and the 20th century. The origins of scientific activity and conservation of Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico "Luigi Pigorini" in Rome, can be traced back to the foundation in 1875 of the "Royal National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography in Rome" within the buildings of the Roman College.

b6880f81-b97a-53a0-8afb-78259cca0821.name: Dolmabahçe Palace
b6880f81-b97a-53a0-8afb-78259cca0821.description: The admiration the Ottoman sultans had for Western monarchs, resulted in the construction of new palaces on the banks of the Bosphorus.

b7735908-2a85-5159-97b8-d8499ee4ac07.name: *A Scene from the Turkish Harem*
b7735908-2a85-5159-97b8-d8499ee4ac07.archival: Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation Collection (Orientalist Paintings Collection)
b7735908-2a85-5159-97b8-d8499ee4ac07.description2: Austrian artists, which were part of the retinue of the Embassy delegation led by Hans Ludwig von Kuefstein that Holy Roman Emperor Ferdinand II sent to Murad IV in 1628, depicted audiences of the delegation, the sultan and his family, various Ottoman garments and intriguing facets of daily life. This painting is possibly a part of such a series. The 1654 inscription over the painting reads, “As it is not customary for distinguished Turkish ladies to leave the house or meet strangers, they invite each other to their homes and amuse themselves with dance, comedy and similar forms of entertainment”. In the lower section of the painting, guests are greeted while women dance to the rhythm of the tambourine. In the upper section, two women are seen dancing with scarves on their heads and embroidered kerchiefs in their hands, accompanied by musicians playing traditional instruments, such as rebab, santur, and tambourine. The carpets, garments and instruments are depicted in elaborate detail.

b7d0545b-be32-5c47-ab91-272824042882.name: Headdress
b7d0545b-be32-5c47-ab91-272824042882.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
b7d0545b-be32-5c47-ab91-272824042882.author: Huda Kilani
b7d0545b-be32-5c47-ab91-272824042882.description2: Line of silver Ottoman coins sewn together on a piece of fabric, part of a headdress. This kind of jewellery was part of the dowry the groom gave to the bride. Dowries consisted mostly of silver jewellery because only the rich could afford gold jewellery. The use of coins as pieces of jewellery in particular was an indirect statement of the financial status of the groom, as brides wore those pieces of jewellery in front of relatives and friends.

b814bde1-48f9-5356-8789-4fecae32bde0.name: Bridal tunic (*Veyke*)
b814bde1-48f9-5356-8789-4fecae32bde0.author: Gordanche Vidinic, ethnologist
b814bde1-48f9-5356-8789-4fecae32bde0.keywords: bridal tunic; embroidery; costume; silver; wedding; marriage
b814bde1-48f9-5356-8789-4fecae32bde0.materials: White canvas, embroidery with variegate threads
b814bde1-48f9-5356-8789-4fecae32bde0.description2: This bridal tunic is abundantly decorated with relief embroidery above the lower hem. The embroidery is very impressive owing to the varied relief techniques applied. It has been created by application of black woollen thread with slight borders in other colours, flat silver string and silver-thread braid. The sleeves are also richly adorned with embroidery in predominantly red nuances. The symbolism of embroidered patterns endow this tunic with universal values distinctive to Macedonian home-made women's attire.

b8a6b459-47fa-5a6f-a12b-76e7e938843b.name: *Parmak cura* (little *cura*)
b8a6b459-47fa-5a6f-a12b-76e7e938843b.description2: The *Cura* is an instrument used by Yörüks (nomads). It is the smallest type of *bağlama* and is usually 55-60cm in length. It generally has three, four, five or six strings and is played either with a quill or the fingers. It is suitable for dynamic dance performances.

b902f002-452f-5bec-8587-b983db9d1182.name: *Schoolboy*
b902f002-452f-5bec-8587-b983db9d1182.keywords: costume; education; school; teaching; travel; traveller; fashion
b902f002-452f-5bec-8587-b983db9d1182.description2: Sheet from *Costumes Turcs*, a lavish set of volumes produced in Turkey for a European audience. They present the appearance of people from different areas, with different jobs etc. A Turkish boy going to school.

b98b5c58-b52f-54a7-85fa-fdea8460caf3.name: *Adornment Of The Bride*
b98b5c58-b52f-54a7-85fa-fdea8460caf3.author: Petar Petrovic
b98b5c58-b52f-54a7-85fa-fdea8460caf3.description2: Bright, folkloristically vivid, technically impeccable and with an abundance of ethnographic detail, this is one of Jovanović’s best paintings, both in this period and as a whole. In a broader sense, this work by Paja Jovanović contains all the relevant characteristics of the poetics of academicism and thus – together with Jovanović’s other works from this period – had a crucial impact on the development of realism in Serbian painting in the late 19th century.

ba42b954-f590-57ca-907e-01a3ca4dde77.name: *Servant*
ba42b954-f590-57ca-907e-01a3ca4dde77.archival: Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation Collection (Orientalist Paintings Collection)
ba42b954-f590-57ca-907e-01a3ca4dde77.description2: The painting depicts a young girl in front of a wall, the lower part of which has been decorated with ceramic tiles with a floral design. The girl is wearing a white dress with embroidery down its front and a long embroidered belt, while her hair is partially covered with a light veil. On the young girl’s chestnut hair there is a gold crown, with gems at its centre. Around her neck she wears a necklace with large gems, a thin bracelet on her left wrist and an armlet on her right arm. The girl is holding a tray on which there is a decanter and cup of blue-and-white porcelain and fruits.

bb542d79-d99d-5291-a57c-0b72137d0e2f.name: Fez of a common soldier of the Austro-Hungarian infantry from Bosnia-Herzegovina
bb542d79-d99d-5291-a57c-0b72137d0e2f.holder: Austrian Military Museum / Institute of Military History
bb542d79-d99d-5291-a57c-0b72137d0e2f.keywords: Fez; Morocco; Tunisia; hat gear; Bosnia; Austrian army; war; warfare; military wear; Ottoman army
bb542d79-d99d-5291-a57c-0b72137d0e2f.description2: The fez was more or less the most significant element of the uniform worn by soldiers of Bosnian-Herzegovinian regiments of the Austro-Hungarian Army, who earned a reputation for bravery and loyalty during World War I. While the fez was in use for all common soldiers, only Muslim officers were allowed to wear the fez instead of the normal black officer's cap. The colour of the fez was changed during the war from red to pike grey.

bc65e295-73e5-5ae4-84e4-1777b2658828.name: Bracelet
bc65e295-73e5-5ae4-84e4-1777b2658828.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
bc65e295-73e5-5ae4-84e4-1777b2658828.author: Huda Kilani
bc65e295-73e5-5ae4-84e4-1777b2658828.keywords: Bedouin; settler; village; economy; dowry; tradition; marriage; Ottoman Jordan
bc65e295-73e5-5ae4-84e4-1777b2658828.description2:
Hollow domes and welded reliefs with locking mechanism. Silver jewellery was the most common, because only rich people could afford gold jewellery. The dowry of silver and gold jewellery was given by the groom to the bride, reflecting the financial status of the groom.  
The Jordanian economy relied on trades and crafts and new waves of people started to come to Jordan and began to settle for these purposes. This object is an example of how traditional fashion reflected the variegated population composition of Jordan in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. It is also an example of local personal attire, fashion, costumes and rites.

be009de4-94db-5ccd-b043-8e9fe6838bd7.name: *Ma'ara*
be009de4-94db-5ccd-b043-8e9fe6838bd7.description2: Gold necklace with blue stones made of oval beads on a gold chain with coin print discs and heart-shaped leaves attached to them, with a large heart-shaped gold pendant inlaid with a blue stone.

bee6cdea-7a07-512a-8073-61c3a5461987.name: *La Sahrienne: Arab dance for piano*
bee6cdea-7a07-512a-8073-61c3a5461987.artist: Composer: P. Codini; illustrator: A. Morel
bee6cdea-7a07-512a-8073-61c3a5461987.description2: The rise of "turkeries" in the 18th century is a good example of the influence of the widespread fascination with the "Orient" on music. In the 19th century, this Orientalism also influenced others art forms, such as painting and photography. Musical motifs started using "oriental" motifs once again in the early 20th century.

bf8ccf55-0b9f-51ab-833d-046d658d52ad.name: *Mahmud II, Sultan of Turkey* (1784–1839)
bf8ccf55-0b9f-51ab-833d-046d658d52ad.keywords: Mahmud II, Sultan of Turkey; Egypt; Janissary; Konya; Ibrahim Pasha; Muhammad Ali; Greece
bf8ccf55-0b9f-51ab-833d-046d658d52ad.description2:
Portrait of Mahmud II, Sultan of Turkey (1784–1839). In 1826 Mahmud II initiated the development of a modern army. This led to the uprising of the Janissary, which was quelled by massacring the rebellious troops. Under Mahmud II's reign, in 1821 the Greeks started their fight for freedom which was granted to them in the Peace of Adrianople in 1829.  
After the destruction of the Janissary, the Ottoman Empire under Sultan Mahmud II had only 35,000 badly trained regular soldiers in 1827. Due to the weakness of the Ottoman Empire, Ibrahim Pasha, the son of Muhammad 'Ali (ruler of Egypt), invaded Syria. On 20 February 1832, the Egyptian Army defeated the Ottoman Army at the Battle of Konya. This forced Mahmud II to sign the Peace of Kütahya and to cede Syria and Kilikia to Egypt.

c1679a4a-eb18-5ec1-bd6f-8c176785d5ff.name: Pendant
c1679a4a-eb18-5ec1-bd6f-8c176785d5ff.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
c1679a4a-eb18-5ec1-bd6f-8c176785d5ff.author: Huda Kilani

c1679a4a-eb18-5ec1-bd6f-8c176785d5ff.description2: A thin silver triangular pendant and welded decoration with blue glass beads. Five chains dangle with Ottoman coins at the end. This kind of jewellery was part of the dowry the groom gave to the bride. Dowries consisted mostly of silver jewellery because only the rich could afford gold jewellery. The use of coins as pieces of jewellery, worn by brides in front of their relatives and friends, was an indirect statement of the financial status of the groom.

c218ec86-d3bb-5c64-b802-3b31940b3669.holder: National Library of Portugal, Digital Library

The narrative focuses on the holy city of Jerusalem, the place of purchase of supposedly true religious relics.

c2865a20-07ed-57a6-a434-0d7f2bfbe970.description: Tunic in cream ground with stencilled decoration in black showing vegetal and geometrical motifs. Some of his designs were inspired in the Orientalism style, he was influenced by his travels and of the historical textiles that he collected.

c2ef4889-9f51-575f-8794-b1fe85502111.name: An Entertainment Scene (Evening entertainment in the Golden Horn) from *Surname-i Vehbi*
c2ef4889-9f51-575f-8794-b1fe85502111.archival: The Library of Sultan Ahmed III
c2ef4889-9f51-575f-8794-b1fe85502111.description2: In this miniature we see an evening of rafts and fireworks on the Golden Horn. The grand vizier is seated on the Aynalıkavak quayside in the right frame and the sultan on the palace balcony. On the first of the two rafts in this procession, dancers and musicians perform in a garden of blazing cypress tree and Solomon’s seal fireworks. On the second is a revolving fortress stuffed with fireworks that have been set off while the military band at the stern of the raft plays.

c3322b4d-5cf0-5412-aee3-1fd52f0cba22.name: Hat (*Cuculj*)
c3322b4d-5cf0-5412-aee3-1fd52f0cba22.author: Milena Petrovic, ethnologist
c3322b4d-5cf0-5412-aee3-1fd52f0cba22.keywords: Headdress; coin; coinage; currency; numismatics; marriage; wedding; costume; textile; fashion
c3322b4d-5cf0-5412-aee3-1fd52f0cba22.materials: Klashna – thick woollen fabric, silver coins, silver alloy. Silversmith's production
c3322b4d-5cf0-5412-aee3-1fd52f0cba22.second_name: Bridal ornament worn on the head
c3322b4d-5cf0-5412-aee3-1fd52f0cba22.description2: In the 19th century and the beginning of the 20th century, metal jewellery and other articles of adornment in Macedonia were made by goldsmiths. They were distinguished with exceptional diversity reflecting the skill and creativity of artisans. This versatility applies particularly to headdresses. The bridal hat is made of broadcloth – *klashna* – which is decorated with small silver coins reminiscent of fish scales. This particular headdress is part of a jewellery set that goes with a piece worn on the breasts, which was called *mingjuska so vot*.

c671443a-8a37-5c35-975f-840074e8db8a.name: *Woman Playing a String Instrument*
c671443a-8a37-5c35-975f-840074e8db8a.archival: Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation Collection (Orientalist Paintings Collection)
c671443a-8a37-5c35-975f-840074e8db8a.keywords: Music; harem; court music; musician; female musician; traditional entertainments
c671443a-8a37-5c35-975f-840074e8db8a.description2: In this painting there is an Ottoman woman in her daily attire with her hair covered by an embroidered and printed kerchief. She plays a string instrument. Music was one of the most popular kinds of amusement in Turkish harems. The lute in particular, and similar string instruments, have always occupied an important place in the lives of women. This picture was used on the cover of a special issue of *Le Figaro Illustré* dedicated to Zonara and published in 1908, and also appeared in *Der'i Se'adet*, a book written by Adolphe Thalasso and illustrated by Zonaro.

c88e4cac-7c3a-5acf-8cad-3a3c6bf1777f.name: Photograph: *Music School, Syria*
c88e4cac-7c3a-5acf-8cad-3a3c6bf1777f.description:
Stereoscopic photography that creates the illusion of depth of field from two apparently identical images mounted on a rigid board by using a specific viewfinder, or stereoscope.  
The images taken by the Keystone View Company show very different scenes related to lifestyles and traditions of different continents. In this case, there is a man playing a stringed instrument with a bow, possibly a type of rebec, surrounded by a group of children and two adults, who watch and listen carefully. In Syria, as in many other parts of the world, music has had and still has an important role as a means of transmitting knowledge and to celebrate individual and collective events, and is closely linked to rites, institutions, cultural and ideological activities of different humans. This image illustrates not only the practice of this activity, music, but also the transfer of knowledge from one generation to another; music serves as a vehicle of expression and relationship between members of a society.

cc3eb98f-be74-5f38-85da-465d5c36d52e.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
cc3eb98f-be74-5f38-85da-465d5c36d52e.author: Huda Kilani
cc3eb98f-be74-5f38-85da-465d5c36d52e.keywords: Ottoman coins; silk cloth; Atlas; cotton
cc3eb98f-be74-5f38-85da-465d5c36d52e.description2: A rectangular piece of Syrian silk cloth (*atlas*) with a small piece of coloured cotton cloth on the front on two sides. There is a line of Ottoman coins sewn together with three tassels dangling at the end with different stones. Silver was the most common jewellery, given by the groom to the bride as dowry. The use of Ottoman coins as pieces of jewellery – shown by women to friends and relatives – was an indirect reference to the financial status of their husbands. Silk was imported from Syria. Its trade in the Syro-Palestinian area was common because of the lack of geographical and political boundaries; some cities were like twins because of their close proximity and exchange of trade goods and business.

cc9708c7-7639-577d-908b-b4db3b0e057e.name: Shéhérazade, a ballet by Michel Fokine. Stage sketch.
cc9708c7-7639-577d-908b-b4db3b0e057e.description2: The Russian choreographer Michel Fokine created the ballet *Shéhérazade* for Rimski-Korsakov's music in Paris in 1910. The tale of Shahrazad was taken from the *One Thousand and One Nights*, which saw constant success in Europe throughout the 19th century.

cda0ca19-8310-53b6-88d9-6a4e2fb00a6f.name: *Medjmouaï teçavir* (Collection de costumes)
cda0ca19-8310-53b6-88d9-6a4e2fb00a6f.keywords: costume; coffee; tobacco; fashion; court life; communication; transportation; travel; traveller; Orientalism
cda0ca19-8310-53b6-88d9-6a4e2fb00a6f.description2: Postcard from Turkey showing the costume worn by various people, according to occupation, activity, etc. Intended for a relatively popular western market. Illustrates the social structures and costumes of the last days of the Ottoman empire. An inspector of the roads. Incidental details of coffee drinking, smoking and French influenced design.

cf7760c0-6a87-5a55-85b5-9801367d91fb.name: Necklace
cf7760c0-6a87-5a55-85b5-9801367d91fb.description: Three strings necklace, with forty-three cylindrical beads of coral, alternating with five spherical silver, tubular finials and smooth; six spherical in silver, with finials decorated with circles of piping and tubular; six biconical accounts also in silver, with tubular trims and cording foot circles; and six ‘*alconciles*’ in silver.

d35ea140-6436-50e0-a3c8-f37c54eabc12.name: Jacket
d35ea140-6436-50e0-a3c8-f37c54eabc12.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
d35ea140-6436-50e0-a3c8-f37c54eabc12.description2: Yusuf Bey Karam's formal jacket, which he wore during his youth. It is made of red velvet with floral patterns embroidered in gilded thread.

d3db70b3-c132-5835-9372-de3aadb98307.name: Bridal outfit (*entari*, long jacket and shoes)
d3db70b3-c132-5835-9372-de3aadb98307.holder: Vehbi Koç Foundation Sadberk Hanim Museum
d3db70b3-c132-5835-9372-de3aadb98307.dimensions: Dress h(front): 140, h (back): 158, sleeves: 55 cm; fleece h: 124, sleeves: 52 cm.
d3db70b3-c132-5835-9372-de3aadb98307.description2: This *entari* (dress) is made of turquoise satin embroidered in various stitches using silver-gilt thread. The bridal outfit is completed by a matching *hırka* (long jacket) made of the same fabric and lined with red fox fur, and matching heeled shoes with uppers of the same fabric and soles made of leather. The tailored bodice of the *entari* is lengthened by flaps of fabric that fall over the skirt, giving the *entari* the appearance of a two-piece skirt and blouse. The front of the bodice is decorated with frills. The skirt flares out from the waist downwards. The scalloped hem is trimmed with a tiny pleated frill. The jacket has a round neck and fitted sleeves, and opens down the front. The shoes are embroidered in silver and decorated at the toe with a blue-tasselled flower.

d6720426-2881-5b4a-8e11-89649a430aa6.name: *Loie Fuller: the serpentine dance*
d6720426-2881-5b4a-8e11-89649a430aa6.description2: Mary Louise Fuller was an American dancer who lived in Europe for many years. As an artist, she was inspired by her travels and by new inventions - the dance of the veils (the "serpentine" dance) mixes Arab influences with light tricks using electricity. Loie Fuller was an important influence in the Art Nouveau and Symbolist movements, and helped train other great artists such as Isadora Duncan. The "serpentine dance" was imitated by many artists, and inspired the first cinematographers, such as the Lumière brothers, who dedicated a short film to it.

d68fb94f-f627-54b5-a330-7d4a6b4992ab.name: Portrait of Shakir Shukayr
d68fb94f-f627-54b5-a330-7d4a6b4992ab.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Hassan El Masri, Remy Nader
d68fb94f-f627-54b5-a330-7d4a6b4992ab.description2: Shakir Shukayr was born in 1850 in Choueifat. He received his primary education here, before moving to the Orthodox School in Suq al-Gharb. He was tutored in Arabic by Shaykh Nasif al-Yaziji, and became a professor first at the Three Doctors School and then at the National School. In 1868 he became a member of the Syriac Scientific Association. Author of numerous books, he died in October 1896.

d698b39b-7d12-5410-a70f-c142ce18b236.name: *Servet-i Fünun* Journal
d698b39b-7d12-5410-a70f-c142ce18b236.description2: This is a magazine published by the authors from the *Servet-ı Fünun* (*Edebiyat-ı Cedide*) movement. It was first published as a scientific magazine by Ahmet İhsan Tokgöz, a pupil of Recaizade Mahmud Ekrem, in 1891. Recaizade Mahmud Ekrem agreed with his pupil to turn this magazine into one of literature, so he arranged that Tevfik Fikret, another student of his from Galatasaray High school, would become head of the literature department. This movement came to an end when the magazine was closed after if published an article entitled “Literature and Justice,” translated by Hüseyin Cahit Yalçın, which was taken as hostile to the governance of Abdülhamid II. Members of the *Edebiyat-ı Cedide* movement remained adherent to Diwan literature due to the political situation of the period as well as political suppression. They were not as open to novelties as the first generation of Tanzimat Era and they adopted art for sake of art.

d7bfd409-e2ad-54bc-aea9-cbf7cee1a22d.name: Bridal jewellery worn on the breasts (*Mingjuska so vot* and necklace)
d7bfd409-e2ad-54bc-aea9-cbf7cee1a22d.author: Milena Petrovic, ethnologist
d7bfd409-e2ad-54bc-aea9-cbf7cee1a22d.keywords: Broad cloth; klashna; coin; coinage; currency; numismatics; textile; costume; wedding; marriage
d7bfd409-e2ad-54bc-aea9-cbf7cee1a22d.materials: Klashna - thick woollen fabric, silver coins, silver alloy, decorative stones, tiny beads - *monistra*
d7bfd409-e2ad-54bc-aea9-cbf7cee1a22d.third_name: Mingjushka so 'vot' – nevestinski ukras za gradi
d7bfd409-e2ad-54bc-aea9-cbf7cee1a22d.description2: This piece of jewellery provides evidence on the versatility of articles of adornment worn by women in Macedonia in the 19th century. *Mingjushka so vot* belongs to the group of jewellery decorating the chests, although there is no clear distinction from pieces worn around the neck. This exquisite breast jewellery consists of a rectangular piece of broadcloth – *klashna* – covered with small silver coins reminiscent of fish scales and adorned with decorative stones. It is bordered by a chain, which is additionally adorned with coins. It used to be worn suspended on a chain. Abundant ornamentation with coins was applied on diverse pieces of jewellery and articles of adornment within all ethnic communities in Macedonia.

d7c8788d-6f4d-5251-abb7-406fabefb7b2.name: *Napoleon returning from the Island of Elba*
d7c8788d-6f4d-5251-abb7-406fabefb7b2.description2: Following his abdication in April 1814 due to his defeat at the hands of the coalition between Austria, Prussia and Russia, Napoléon was exiled to Elba, a French territory at the time. He then unexpectedly disembarked at Antibes (France) on 1 March 1815, accompanied by a small army, and went on to take control of Grenoble, Lyon, and finally Paris. King Louis XVIII fled, and Napoléon temporarily regained the throne (the "Hundred Days"), until his defeat at Waterloo marked his final abdication. This image contributed to the myth of Napoléon, illustrating the emperor's determination during his journey from Elba to Paris, also known as the "Vol de l'Aigle" (flight of the eagle).

d9278f88-7c6f-5ba2-a99d-94b0d6496626.name: Portrait Album – Ottoman State Officers
d9278f88-7c6f-5ba2-a99d-94b0d6496626.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
d9278f88-7c6f-5ba2-a99d-94b0d6496626.dates: Late 19th century – beginning of the 20th century
d9278f88-7c6f-5ba2-a99d-94b0d6496626.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Fotoğraf; Eski Istanbul; Nikolas Andriomenos
d9278f88-7c6f-5ba2-a99d-94b0d6496626.description2: With the political developments of the 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. As a result, close to 160 artists visited Istanbul in the 19th century. Born in Costantinople in 1851, Nicolas Andriomenos was an Ottoman Greek who learned photography in the 1870s from Cosmi Abdullah. At that time, Cosmi operated a studio of his own in Beyazıt, but turned the business over to Andriomenos in late 1879, after which its new proprietor soon made it into one of the city's most prestigious portrait studios.

d92eefc6-b8cb-57be-9e74-3bd00aa19302.name: *Théâtre de l'Opéra. "Aida". Avenue of the sphinxes at the gates of Thebes (act 2 scene 2)*
d92eefc6-b8cb-57be-9e74-3bd00aa19302.artist: Engraver: F. Moller; artists: Henry Scott, Jean-Baptiste Lavastre
d92eefc6-b8cb-57be-9e74-3bd00aa19302.description2: Commissioned by Isma'il Pasha for the inauguration of the Suez Canal, Verdi's opera *Aida* was performed for the first time in Cairo in 1871, with great success. It recreated life at the time of the pharaohs, with the details and the plot developed by the archaeologist Mariette. *Aida* was performed in Paris from 1876, with a grand and successful performance at the Opéra Garnier in 1880.

d9708463-f720-5673-ac88-cf01adf12b47.name: *Portrait of a Greek Wearing a Fustanela*
d9708463-f720-5673-ac88-cf01adf12b47.author: Tsigakou 1984, 195
d9708463-f720-5673-ac88-cf01adf12b47.description2: It may depict a notable of Aighion, Andreas Londos (1786–1846) who entertained Lord Byron on his first visit to Greece. The picture is similar in style, setting and pose to that entitled ‘Un Grec de Janina’ in Dupré’s *Voyage à Athènes et Constantinople*, 1825. Louis Dupré (1798–1837) was one of the most talented painters who travelled to Greece. He arrived in 1819. The French artist who was an ardent philhellene published in 1825 a set of coloured lithographs of views and studies of costumes from Greece, entitled *Voyage a Athènes et Constantinople*.

dbf4dc13-3f6b-5da9-bf05-cfabe7876ad3.name: Headdress
dbf4dc13-3f6b-5da9-bf05-cfabe7876ad3.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
dbf4dc13-3f6b-5da9-bf05-cfabe7876ad3.author: Huda Kilani
dbf4dc13-3f6b-5da9-bf05-cfabe7876ad3.description2: A silver circular disk with inherent decorations in the carving, and prominent dome above; chains dangling with oval shapes at the end. With two different length. This ornament was placed on the top of a high hat worn by al-Druze (Druse) women. Silver was the most common jewellery. The dowry of silver and gold jewellery was given by the groom to the bride, reflecting the financial status of the groom. This object illustrates the variegated social composition and the demographic changes in the Jordanian territory in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. The al-Druze tribes migrated from Syria (Hawran) to north east Jordan in the early twentieth century because of their support for the Syrian revolution against the French occupation.

dcf06086-9092-5d9d-bf04-d94e167662b6.name: Turkish women
dcf06086-9092-5d9d-bf04-d94e167662b6.description2: The Zangaki brothers were a pair of photographers working in Egypt who sold "Orientalist" photos to Western toursits, allowing them to immortalise their trip to the "Orient". This photograph shows two Turkish women, probably mother and daughter, in formal dress.

ddd75581-2e37-5baa-8483-63c54f368af5.name: Dress
ddd75581-2e37-5baa-8483-63c54f368af5.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
ddd75581-2e37-5baa-8483-63c54f368af5.author: Huda Kilani
ddd75581-2e37-5baa-8483-63c54f368af5.description2: Long black silk dress (*malas*), narrow at the waist, wide at the bottom, embroidered with cross-stitch dark blue and red on the chest and on the front side, worn by women of the al-Druze tribes, with a shirt underneath. This object illustrates the variegated composition and the demographic changes of the Jordan population in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. It also shows how the different populations brought with them their fashion, costumes and rites which contributed to the multifaceted social and cultural heritage of Jordan. The al-Druze tribes migrated from Syria (Hawran) to northeast Jordan in the early twentieth century because of their support for the Syrian revolution against the French occupation.

df6c527d-f54f-5563-b918-6ec2da8e94f9.name: Tunic (*'aba'a*)
df6c527d-f54f-5563-b918-6ec2da8e94f9.description: Tunic in cotton gauze lined in a red satin. The printed decoration is similar to the Venetian Renaissance printed velvets. This garment is part of the assemble inspired in the travels to North Africa made by Fortuny.
df6c527d-f54f-5563-b918-6ec2da8e94f9.holder: Museum of Costume, Ethnographical Heritage Research Centre
df6c527d-f54f-5563-b918-6ec2da8e94f9.author: Elvira González

dfd2eeea-301b-506a-85f9-f9ad927ce8f2.name: Dress
dfd2eeea-301b-506a-85f9-f9ad927ce8f2.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
dfd2eeea-301b-506a-85f9-f9ad927ce8f2.author: Huda Kilani
dfd2eeea-301b-506a-85f9-f9ad927ce8f2.keywords: Dress; machine embroidery; patterns; custmes and rites; Ottoman coins
dfd2eeea-301b-506a-85f9-f9ad927ce8f2.materials: Chinese cotton, silver coins; machine weaving, machine embroidery
dfd2eeea-301b-506a-85f9-f9ad927ce8f2.description2: Women's costumes of the central regions of Jordan are characterized by length, dark colours, light vertical strips of embroidery and very long sleeves. This black and blue dress has a very loose fitting, open chest and long flared sleeves pulled over a head band. The length of the dress was adjusted to the height of the woman by a sash. Wide at the bottom, it is decorated horizontally with blue cotton stripes and vertically with embroidery lines and Ottoman coins. The traditional costumes reflect the variegated population composition and demographic changes of the late 19th century-early 20th century Jordanian territory, when new waves of people arrived and settled for the purpose of trades and crafts. Craft was not limited to the everyday life and the profits from crafts were a source of income.

dff63501-6388-5281-9baf-bb1a3d253e7f.name: Rababa
dff63501-6388-5281-9baf-bb1a3d253e7f.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
dff63501-6388-5281-9baf-bb1a3d253e7f.author: Huda Kilani
dff63501-6388-5281-9baf-bb1a3d253e7f.keywords: goats gut; animals skin; horse hair
dff63501-6388-5281-9baf-bb1a3d253e7f.materials: Wood, animals skin; handmade and hand painted
dff63501-6388-5281-9baf-bb1a3d253e7f.description2: Four pieces of wood formed into a rectangular shape; the top and bottom are covered with animal skin and joined with goat’s intestines. The rababa is played with a bow consisting of an arched stick with horse hair. The rababa is a musical instrument widely used in the Bedouin tradition. Music played in communal setting is an essential part of the traditions in Bedouin communities for leisure at communal gatherings.

e055e6ed-ffba-5b33-a42a-7f9060dc3802.name: Paul Draneht, his wife Adele Casati and their daughter Despina
e055e6ed-ffba-5b33-a42a-7f9060dc3802.author: Massimiliano Cremona, Ignazio Galella
e055e6ed-ffba-5b33-a42a-7f9060dc3802.description2:
Paul Draneht (1815-1894) was born in Nicosia (Cyprus) as Pavlos Pavlidis. He was the child of a Greek Christian Orthodox family who fled Cyprus to escape the clashes between Greeks and Turks and then took refuge in Egypt.  
The Khedive of Egypt sent him to study in France. He later had a brilliant career in service to the Khedive participating in the negotiations on the opening of the Suez Canal. He became superintendent of the Egyptian Opera Theatre and commissioned the opera Aida to the Italian composer Giuseppe Verdi.  
Paul Draneht married Adelaide Casati, the daughter of a cello player who performed at the Aida premiere. Their daughter Despina Draneht married a Greek businessman, Emmanuel Zervudachi.

e396b7b2-cb07-51d7-86f1-b131b11dbfe2.name: Portrait of a lady of the court playing the tambourine
e396b7b2-cb07-51d7-86f1-b131b11dbfe2.archival: Orientalist Paintings Collection-Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation Collection
e396b7b2-cb07-51d7-86f1-b131b11dbfe2.keywords: Pierre Desire Guillemet; Orientalism; painting; İstanbul
e396b7b2-cb07-51d7-86f1-b131b11dbfe2.description2: This painting is one of the four half-length portraits painted by Pierre Désiré Guillemet in 1874-1875 depicting a young woman of the Ottoman Court. Her dress has been emphasized by means of a neutral background. She is wearing a *dört etek* (four-skirted) robe, made of *savai* fabric. Part of her undershirt with embroidered borders is visible from her large sleeves and around the edges of the robe. Her robe has a floral pattern with lively colours and her belt has a clasp with a two large stones in a silver setting. Her chestnut-coloured hair flows down to her shoulder. She wears two strands of pearls around her neck and a gold earing with pearls and gems. On her head she wears a cap of blue fabric decorated with small white flowers, plumes and toile.

e3bca328-205b-530c-8cb6-99cd21d8c8dd.name: *Two Musician Girls*
e3bca328-205b-530c-8cb6-99cd21d8c8dd.archival: Orientalist Paintings Collection-Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation Collection
e3bca328-205b-530c-8cb6-99cd21d8c8dd.keywords: Osman Hamdi Bey; Orientalism; painting; İstanbul
e3bca328-205b-530c-8cb6-99cd21d8c8dd.description2: As opposed to the Western Orientalists who emphasize sexuality in their female figures, in Osman Hamdi’s paintings the female figures are often conscious of the period of Westernization in the Ottoman Empire, as well as their individual identities and talents, and are thus open to learning and self-development. In a number of Osman Hamdi’s works, the Ottoman woman is portrayed playing an instrument or reading and she always appears fully clothed. In this painting, which incorporates architectural elements of the Bursa Green Mosque, apart from musical instruments like the *tambur* (lute) and the tambourine, Ottoman decorative elements such as rugs, woodwork, stone carving, and tiles complement the artist’s unique approach to the female identity.

e3f48d7b-3bf0-5b73-ae59-24ec80351340.name: Tantur (woman's headdress)
e3f48d7b-3bf0-5b73-ae59-24ec80351340.holder: National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography “Luigi Pigorini”
e3f48d7b-3bf0-5b73-ae59-24ec80351340.author: Vito Lattanzi, Marina Minozzi
e3f48d7b-3bf0-5b73-ae59-24ec80351340.keywords: Woman; photograph; anthropology; ethnology; geography; travel; ethnography; museums; model; genre picture; portrait; representation of the other; costume; material culture; collection; Lebanon; floral decoration; animal decoration; zoomorphism; zoomorphic
e3f48d7b-3bf0-5b73-ae59-24ec80351340.materials: Silver laminate decorated with embossed work
e3f48d7b-3bf0-5b73-ae59-24ec80351340.description2: The Tantur is an example of cultural tradition developed inside the contaminations typical of the Mediterranean world. It is decorated with symbolic images of leaves, flowers and animals and it is engraved with the year of Egira, 1172. Its cylindrical shape is reminiscent of an *asherah*, one of the emblems of the Phoenician goddess of fertility Astarte (the Siriac Atargotis), often represented with cylindrical headgear. The origins in terms of scientific activity and conservation of Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico "Luigi Pigorini" in Rome, can be traced back to the foundation in 1875 of the "Royal National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography in Rome" within the buildings of the Roman College.

e50ae40d-d2e5-50ff-9f8d-f861d8f298d4.name: *Woman from Constantine*
e50ae40d-d2e5-50ff-9f8d-f861d8f298d4.author: Dalila Orfali
e50ae40d-d2e5-50ff-9f8d-f861d8f298d4.description2: This painting belonged first to the collection at St. Martin's Church, Cologne, then to the Duchess of Reggio. It can be found in the catalogue written by the art historian Léonce Bénédite on Chassériau (see vol. 2, p. 495; cf. André Dezarrois, *Théodore Chassériau, sa Vie et son Œuvre*). The artist used women from the Jewish community in Constantine as models for woman's face and dress, following Dehodencq's example from his time in Morocco. This explains her resemblance to Rachel's portrait, which is also kept in the museum.

e71cbefd-c4b2-5e4b-a2b6-9dd7a89e735f.name: Portrait of Doctor Rashid al-Dahdah
e71cbefd-c4b2-5e4b-a2b6-9dd7a89e735f.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Hassan El Masri, Remy Nader
e71cbefd-c4b2-5e4b-a2b6-9dd7a89e735f.description2: Rashid al-Dahdah was born in 'Armun in 1813. He studied first at 'Ayn Warka School, and then at Bzummar monastery. He worked first as a secretary, before moving to Saida in 1843 where he studied Islamic law. He later moved to France (Marseille and Paris), where he founded a newspaper in both French and Arabic. Author of numerous books, he died in May 1889 in France.

e733f2a6-8940-5e1d-ba96-bb338e5c87f6.name: Hooded cloak (*burnus*)
e733f2a6-8940-5e1d-ba96-bb338e5c87f6.description: Cloak in green velvet with stencilled decoration of pomegranates and leaves in brown. This velvet is based on the Venetian ones of the 15th and 16th centuries. The cloak has a wide fullness at the bottom and a big hood, formed by four points. The cloak is lined in a green silk, printed in silver vegetal motifs.
e733f2a6-8940-5e1d-ba96-bb338e5c87f6.holder: Museum of Costume, Ethnographical Heritage Research Centre
e733f2a6-8940-5e1d-ba96-bb338e5c87f6.author: Elvira González

e76f2cd3-86ac-51b9-b076-e4ec90a04fbc.name: *Illustrations of the One Thousand and One Nights, vol. 1*
e76f2cd3-86ac-51b9-b076-e4ec90a04fbc.description2: The *One Thousand and One Nights* played an important role in bringing the East and the West closer together. Galland was its first French translator, translating with much liberty what he had been able to understand in the early 18th century. The translated *One Thousand and One Nights* were extremely successful, and became the subject of a variety of art forms, both allowing Europeans to become better acquainted with the Arab world, but also forming the basis for lasting stereotypes.

e826dd7d-b40a-53fb-88ca-e2af297d1f40.name: Jacket
e826dd7d-b40a-53fb-88ca-e2af297d1f40.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
e826dd7d-b40a-53fb-88ca-e2af297d1f40.description2: Yusuf Bey Karam's jacket, probably worn during the summer months. It has short sleeves and is made of a dark blue fabric, with floral patterns embroidered in gilded thread.

e84c1d50-6a52-5437-9881-f6dd95677f63.name: Doctor and author Tawfīq Kanʻān, three-quarter length portrait, standing, facing front, in uniform
e84c1d50-6a52-5437-9881-f6dd95677f63.materials: Photographic print on cabinet card mount

ec198745-bf85-5cf3-a025-264676b49e2d.name: *Histoire de la Princesse Boudour (Conte des mille et une nuits)*, Translation by J.C. Mardrus of *The Story of the Princess Boudour: Tales of a Thousand and One Nights*
ec198745-bf85-5cf3-a025-264676b49e2d.description: François-Louis Schmied (1873–1941) and Jean Dunand (1877–1942) worked together on *Histoire de la Princess Boudour*, the French translation of one of the tales from *The Arabian Nights* by J.-C- Mardrus. The painter, illustrator, engraver, bookbinder and publisher François-Louis Schmied was primarily responsible for producing the graphic design and handling of the text, the illustrations and their wood interpretations. Dunand produced a lacquered metal plaque that transmitted the eroticism and voluptuousness revealed throughout the text. Using warm colours, Princess Boudour is portrayed on a red ground sprinkled with gold, and appears as a very elongated, tubular figure holding a flower with both hands. It’s a limited edition, just twenty copies, it’s a extremely rare Art Deco book.
ec198745-bf85-5cf3-a025-264676b49e2d.author: Manuela Fidalgo
ec198745-bf85-5cf3-a025-264676b49e2d.keywords: Orientalism; Literature;  François – Louis Schmeed; Jean Dunand George
ec198745-bf85-5cf3-a025-264676b49e2d.materials: Binding: black and green morocco by Georges Bretté (1893–1969), with one lacquered plate by Jean Dunond (1877–1942)

en: Carvalho, Pedro Moura (ed), *The World of Lacquer. 2000 years of History*, exhibition catalogue, Lisbon: Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation, 2001, p.241.

f0667100-6159-569b-9a0e-84fec1b968f0.name: Headdress
f0667100-6159-569b-9a0e-84fec1b968f0.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
f0667100-6159-569b-9a0e-84fec1b968f0.author: Huda Kilani
f0667100-6159-569b-9a0e-84fec1b968f0.keywords: Ottoman; Russian coins; pendent; red and green silk
f0667100-6159-569b-9a0e-84fec1b968f0.materials: Silver, fabric, glass beads, coins; casting, welding, weaving
f0667100-6159-569b-9a0e-84fec1b968f0.description2: Three bands of silver chain fitted around the sides and over the crown of the head and attached to a surrounding fabric patterned in minute beadwork and sewn with various Ottoman and Russian coins. From this head-piece hangs a long piece of cotton sewn with coins of the Ottoman Empire with a rectangular pendant and multiple red and green silk tassels on the back. Headdresses like this one were worn by married women, as silver was the most common jewellery. The dowry of silver and gold jewellery was given by the groom to the bride. The Ottoman and Russian coins reflect the social and economic situation of Jordan between the end of the 19th century and the early 20th century, when it was part of the Ottoman empire and it was influenced by population movements, demographic changes and trade with distant countries.

f1858928-5bad-513c-bdc1-bfdf93efecdb.name: Pair of boots (*tmeg*)
f1858928-5bad-513c-bdc1-bfdf93efecdb.description: A pair of Boots (*tmeg*) crafted in Meknès in the 19th century, but making use of British imports such as velvet (*nta‘a*) and gold thread.

f22befb9-5e91-59ad-a5d6-b1b4804da1d6.name: *Fête Égyptienne: Divertissement de Concert pour Piano: op. 3*
f22befb9-5e91-59ad-a5d6-b1b4804da1d6.artist: Composer: Angelo Dal Vesco; Illustrator: L. Denis
f22befb9-5e91-59ad-a5d6-b1b4804da1d6.description2: French "Egyptomania", which began with the campaign in Egypt and lasted the whole 19th century, saw a period of particular intensity during the construction of the Suez Canal. The illustrator of this score, responding to the music's supposedly Egyptian inspiration, focused his illustrations on stereotypical Egyptian images (pyramids, sphinx, palm trees), but notably failed to include images of Egyptian people or daily life.

f23c34bf-814d-5e9e-8baf-ebe84ce157b4.name: *Folies Rambuteau. New quartet from the Auvergne.*
f23c34bf-814d-5e9e-8baf-ebe84ce157b4.description2: The 19th century saw mass rural to urban migration, particularly to Paris, for largely economic reasons. These migrants often settled with people from their region, who offered them work in specific fields. Thus, those from the Savoy region became specialised in chimney-sweeping, those from the Auvergne were water-carriers or coal-merchants, those from Brittany were domestic workers, and so on. Regional solidarity therefore ensured the survival of regional culture. In this image, for example, a quartet from the Auvergne are advertising their performance in a *café-concert* in traditional dress. Music from the Auvergne was the origin of the Parisian *bal-musette* (a dance accompanied by accordion music).

f310be0c-2e4a-5a7a-ab0c-baaa41091e32.name: *Dokhla* (wedding dress)
f310be0c-2e4a-5a7a-ab0c-baaa41091e32.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
f310be0c-2e4a-5a7a-ab0c-baaa41091e32.keywords: Embroidery from Nabeul; sequins and gold thread
f310be0c-2e4a-5a7a-ab0c-baaa41091e32.materials: Embroidered fabric with gold-plated silver thread
f310be0c-2e4a-5a7a-ab0c-baaa41091e32.description2: This tunic is entirely embroidered with gold-plated silver thread. This is the most important element of the marriage ceremony (jelwa) in Nabeul (Tunisia). The rectangular tunic's splendour comes from its incredibly rich embroidery, which is made of various different silk ribbons, all embellished with tal. In fact, the embroidery entirely covers the fabric itself. The breast and belt areas are embroidered with sequins and gold thread. The tunic is calf-length, and a luxurious pair of silk trousers can be seen beneath, covered in gold embroidery to match the sleeves. In addition to this, one of the bride's many items of jewellery is a great chain of golden rings, a rihana, which she wears with a large necklace made of a scented material. Lastly, the bride's head is covered by an embroidered veil made of muslin and silk.

f5eca8aa-876e-503f-b619-df15835f81aa.name: Necklace
f5eca8aa-876e-503f-b619-df15835f81aa.holder: Musée Public National des Arts et Traditions Populaires
f5eca8aa-876e-503f-b619-df15835f81aa.description2: This silver necklace from Grande Kabylie was traditionally worn on a woman's bosom to hold the *ddill*, a finely woven cloth worn by women of the region. It is made of of two ornate brooches with a coral in the centre, connected by a gold chain necklace to which the jeweller has added various French coins (francs) that were no longer in use. A number of jewellers used coins to decorate their jewellery. They usually used coins which had suddenly gone out of use.

f7033496-607e-547b-91fa-2429e3eba90a.name: Portrait of Nawfal Ni'mat Allah Nawfal
f7033496-607e-547b-91fa-2429e3eba90a.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Hassan El Masri, Remy Nader
f7033496-607e-547b-91fa-2429e3eba90a.description2: Nawfal Ni'mat Allah Nawfal was born in Tripoli in 1812. He studied first in Tripoli then in Egypt, after moving there with his father. In 1828 he returned to Lebanon and was hired as an accountant in the wilayat of Tripoli. He remained in this post for seven years, before moving briefly to Beirut and then back to Tripoli. Upon his death, he donated his vast library to the Syrian Protestant College (now the American University of Beirut). He wrote several books on literature, and had many articles published in popular contemporary newspapers, such as *Lisasn al-Hal*. He died in 1887.

f8c2bcec-57eb-5f11-8bfe-5d3461e46436.name: Lute
f8c2bcec-57eb-5f11-8bfe-5d3461e46436.description:
Plucked instrument with four double orders. The headstock is inlaid with silver motifs. It has eight round pins decorated with flowers which end in bone buttons. The nut is also made of bone. The fingerboard is adorned with marquetry and inlay work and has been partially restored; it has no frets.  
The lid is decorated with a quite flamboyant pierced rosette. The bridge is made of bone and wood with stars decoration. The wavy tailpiece is made of wood. The neck is decorated with marquetry in two colours forming a zigzag. The soundboard is concave and consists of eleven staves.

f936f85a-a23f-55c1-ba78-3750eb672753.name: Portrait of Hajj Husayn Bayham
f936f85a-a23f-55c1-ba78-3750eb672753.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Hassan El Masri, Remy Nader
f936f85a-a23f-55c1-ba78-3750eb672753.description2: Born in Beirut in 1833, Hajj Husayn Bayham studied under great masters such as Shaykh 'Abd Allah Khalid and Shaykh Muhammad al-Hut. He mainly worked in public posts, including the council of the wilayet of Saida, the tribunal of commerce and the municipal council. He also wrote poetry in his spare time and had a vast collection of works in his private library. In 1878 he was elected to represent Beirut in the Ottoman parliament. He died in 1881.

f9783bd6-7a5b-5ca2-8a70-781a2af32872.name: Cross chain
f9783bd6-7a5b-5ca2-8a70-781a2af32872.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
f9783bd6-7a5b-5ca2-8a70-781a2af32872.author: Huda Kilani
f9783bd6-7a5b-5ca2-8a70-781a2af32872.description2: A cross of silver on a silver chain known with the folkloric name “heal of gazelle”, worn by Christian women. Silver was the most common jewellery; only rich people used gold. The dowry of silver and gold jewellery was given by the groom to the bride, reflecting the financial status of the groom. This object illustrates the variegated religious composition of Jordan in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. It also demonstrates personal attire, fashion, local costumes and rites.

f9788b95-591f-522c-bd57-84003553fdd9.name: *Üçetek entari*
f9788b95-591f-522c-bd57-84003553fdd9.holder: Vehbi Koç Foundation Sadberk Hanim Museum
f9788b95-591f-522c-bd57-84003553fdd9.description2: The attire of Ottoman women included dresses for the outdoors and the indoors. Starting from early 19th century, dresses called *üçetek* (dress with three skirts) and *dörtetek* (dress with four skirts) became fashionable. As relations with Europe increased, women in Istanbul started to use imported European textiles for their new dresses. This *üçetek entari* (dress with three skirts) is made of a soft red-coloured *canfes* (fine-textured shiny silk fabric) embroidered in the laid cord technique. The robe has a long trailing skirt, wrist-length sleeves and a stand-up collar. It fastens across the chest with button loops and plaited buttons. Along the edges of the skirt, sleeves, slits and seams are undulating floral designs embroidered in coloured silk cord.

f99fda0f-bbfe-5494-9147-d4cccb13620e.name: *Théâtre du Châtelet. Germinal*
f99fda0f-bbfe-5494-9147-d4cccb13620e.description2: The thirteenth novel in the *Rougon-Macquart* series, *Germinal* (1885), is the most well-known and the most discussed of Zola's works. This naturalist writer took a new approach to depicting workers' lives, shedding light on miners' terrible working conditions and the violence and difficulty of strikes. Fearing that the adaptation of this novel for stage would trigger social unrest, the play was initially banned. It was finally performed for the first time in 1888 at the Théâtre du Châtelet. This poster highlights the most important themes of the novel - life in the mine, strikes, etc.

f9ae9656-29ab-534b-a02c-90fe95d65205.name: Three pairs of clogs
f9ae9656-29ab-534b-a02c-90fe95d65205.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
f9ae9656-29ab-534b-a02c-90fe95d65205.description2: Wooden clogs such as these have a long history in the Middle East, emerging before the Middle Ages and remaining popular for centuries to come. They were made of a variety of woods, including walnut, apricot, willow, poplar, or beech. The wood was cut into wedge shapes then moulded around the foot of the wearer. Excess wood was then shaved off, the heel attached, and the wood painted and polished. Leather girdles in a variety of colours were fixed to the heel with special nails and the wood would often be decorated with mosaics of bone or seashells organised in geometric or floral patterns. These shoes were designed to be comfortable and resistant to water, and thus were usually worn at home, particularly by women.

f9c5a022-ba1e-5b5b-a490-3b54263c0271.name: *Daffah khachyya*
f9c5a022-ba1e-5b5b-a490-3b54263c0271.description2: This was purchased from Sheikh Sa\`ud’s family collection in 2001. The cloak is handmade and hand embroidered, made from heavy black wool. It is estimated to be older than 1960, between the 1940’s and the 1950’s. It is speculated that it was used by the Bedouins from eastern Saudi Arabia. It is called *daffah khachyya* and not *bisht*. *Khachyya* is the man who would have been involved in making the cloaks.

fa113d57-874f-5262-96a7-d769cd7f7fd8.description: *Djellaba* made in tabby or plain weave, with a striped decoration from the different wefts thread colours. The origin of this design was travels by Fortuny to North Africa in the 1930s.

fc5492b4-b79e-5ab6-acf3-8e4d44f66cbc.name: The villa of Paul Draneht in Oggebbio (Verbania, Italy)
fc5492b4-b79e-5ab6-acf3-8e4d44f66cbc.author: Massimiliano Cremona, Ignazio Galella
fc5492b4-b79e-5ab6-acf3-8e4d44f66cbc.archival: Intra: Tipografia Intrese, no date (but postal stamp of 1906)
fc5492b4-b79e-5ab6-acf3-8e4d44f66cbc.description2:
In 1872, Paul Draneht Bey bought a Villa on the Lago Maggiore (Italy), which he remodelled, mixing oriental and European architectural styles. From this postcard, one can see a tower with an Arabic flavour.  
In the interior, there was an “Egyptian hall”, modelled according to the style of an ancient Upper-Egypt temple. The furniture was made by one of the shops in Paris that was making the scenes for the opera *Aida*.
